+fn owned_plan_record_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str, plan_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
+    paths
+        .job_dir(job_id)
+        .join("owned-plans")
+        .join(format!("{plan_id}.json"))
+}
+
+fn record_owned_plan(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    root_plan_id: &str,
+    plan: &deadreckon_core::plan::Plan,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let Some(job_id) = plan.owner_job_id.as_deref() else {
+        return Ok(());
+    };
+    let record = OwnedPlanRecord {
+        schema_version: 1,
+        job_id: job_id.to_string(),
+        root_plan_id: root_plan_id.to_string(),
+        plan_id: plan.plan_id.clone(),
+        parent_plan_id: plan.parent_plan_id.clone(),
+        immutable_definition_sha256: immutable_plan_sha256(plan)?,
+        recorded_at: Utc::now(),
+    };
+    let path = owned_plan_record_path(paths, job_id, &plan.plan_id);
+    if path.is_file() {
+        let existing: OwnedPlanRecord = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path)?)?;
+        if existing.job_id != record.job_id
+            || existing.root_plan_id != record.root_plan_id
+            || existing.plan_id != record.plan_id
+            || existing.parent_plan_id != record.parent_plan_id
+            || existing.immutable_definition_sha256 != record.immutable_definition_sha256
+        {
+            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                "protected ownership definition changed for Plan {}",
+                plan.plan_id
+            ))));
+        }
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    commands::job::write_json_synced(&path, &record)
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn record_owned_plan_tree(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    root: &deadreckon_core::plan::Plan,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    if root.owner_job_id.is_none() {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    let root_plan_id = root.plan_id.clone();
+    let mut pending = vec![root.clone()];
+    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
+    while let Some(plan) = pending.pop() {
+        if !seen.insert(plan.plan_id.clone()) {
+            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                "owned Plan tree contains a cycle at {}",
+                plan.plan_id
+            ))));
+        }
+        if plan.owner_job_id != root.owner_job_id {
+            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                "subplan {} does not retain root Job owner",
+                plan.plan_id
+            ))));
+        }
+        record_owned_plan(paths, &root_plan_id, &plan)?;
+        for task in &plan.tasks {
+            let Some(subplan_id) = task.subplan.as_deref() else {
+                continue;
+            };
+            let child = deadreckon_core::load_plan(paths, subplan_id)?;
+            if child.parent_plan_id.as_deref() != Some(plan.plan_id.as_str()) {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                    "subplan {subplan_id} does not point back to parent {}",
+                    plan.plan_id
+                ))));
+            }
+            pending.push(child);
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn validate_owned_plan_if_present(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    plan_id: &str,
+    job_id: &str,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    if !paths.plan_json(plan_id).is_file() {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    let plan = deadreckon_core::load_plan(paths, plan_id)?;
+    let path = owned_plan_record_path(paths, job_id, plan_id);
+    let record: OwnedPlanRecord = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path).map_err(|source| {
+        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::Io {
+            path: path.clone(),
+            source,
+        })
+    })?)?;
+    if record.job_id != job_id
+        || record.plan_id != plan_id
+        || record.parent_plan_id != plan.parent_plan_id
+        || record.immutable_definition_sha256 != immutable_plan_sha256(&plan)?
+    {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "Plan {plan_id} no longer matches its protected Job-owned definition"
+        ))));
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn delegation_pending_path(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job_id: &str,
+    capability_id: &str,
+) -> PathBuf {
+    paths
+        .job_dir(job_id)
+        .join("delegations")
+        .join("pending")
+        .join(format!("{capability_id}.json"))
+}
+
+fn delegation_consumed_path(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job_id: &str,
+    capability_id: &str,
+) -> PathBuf {
+    paths
+        .job_dir(job_id)
+        .join("delegations")
+        .join("consumed")
+        .join(format!("{capability_id}.json"))
+}
+
+fn invocation_argv_sha256(argv: &[String]) -> Result<String> {
+    Ok(deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(
+        &serde_json::to_string(argv)?,
+    ))
+}
+
+fn canonical_invocation_path(path: &Path, label: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
+    fs::canonicalize(path).map_err(|source| {
+        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "delegated {label} path {} is unavailable: {source}",
+            path.display()
+        )))
+    })
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn prepare_delegated_invocation(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    action: DelegatedAction,
+    argv: &[String],
+    cwd: &Path,
+    scope_root: &Path,
+    plan: Option<&deadreckon_core::plan::Plan>,
+) -> Result<PreparedDelegation> {
+    let context = DRIVER_CONTEXT.get().ok_or_else(|| {
+        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "only an authenticated Job driver can delegate executable work".to_string(),
+        ))
+    })?;
+    if !commands::supervisor::guarded_driver_authority_is_live(paths, &context.authority)? {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "the Job driver cannot delegate work without a current fenced lease".to_string(),
+        )));
+    }
+    let immutable_plan_sha256 = if let Some(plan) = plan {
+        let owner = resolve_plan_owner(paths, plan)?.ok_or_else(|| {
+            CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                "Plan {} has no durable Job owner",
+                plan.plan_id
+            )))
+        })?;
+        if owner.job.job_id.as_ref() != context.job_id {
+            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                "Plan {} belongs to Job {}, not current Job {}",
+                plan.plan_id, owner.job.job_id, context.job_id
+            ))));
+        }
+        validate_owned_plan_if_present(paths, &plan.plan_id, &context.job_id)?;
+        Some(immutable_plan_sha256(plan)?)
+    } else {
+        None
+    };
+    let capability_id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
+    let token = format!("{capability_id}:{}", Uuid::new_v4());
+    let record = DelegatedInvocation {
+        schema_version: 1,
+        capability_id: capability_id.clone(),
+        job_id: context.job_id.clone(),
+        authority: context.authority.clone(),
+        action,
+        immutable_plan_sha256,
+        argv_sha256: invocation_argv_sha256(argv)?,
+        cwd: canonical_invocation_path(cwd, "working directory")?,
+        scope_root: canonical_invocation_path(scope_root, "scope root")?,
+        token_sha256: deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(&token),
+        issued_at: Utc::now(),
+    };
+    commands::job::write_json_synced(
+        &delegation_pending_path(paths, &context.job_id, &capability_id),
+        &record,
+    )?;
+    Ok(PreparedDelegation {
+        capability_id,
+        job_id: context.job_id.clone(),
+        token,
+    })
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn apply_delegation(command: &mut Command, prepared: &PreparedDelegation) {
+    command
+        .env(DELEGATION_JOB_ENV, &prepared.job_id)
+        .env(DELEGATION_ID_ENV, &prepared.capability_id)
+        .stdin(Stdio::piped());
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn release_delegation(child: &mut Child, prepared: &PreparedDelegation) -> Result<()> {
+    let mut input = child.stdin.take().ok_or_else(|| {
+        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "delegated child did not expose its private capability pipe".to_string(),
+        ))
+    })?;
+    input.write_all(prepared.token.as_bytes())?;
+    input.write_all(b"\n")?;
+    input.flush()?;
+    drop(input);
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn validate_delegated_action(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    record: &DelegatedInvocation,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    match &record.action {
+        DelegatedAction::PlanChild {
+            plan_id,
+            task_id,
+            task_index,
+            task_attempt,
+        } => {
+            let plan = deadreckon_core::load_plan(paths, plan_id)?;
+            let owner = resolve_plan_owner(paths, &plan)?.ok_or_else(|| {
+                CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated child Plan is no longer Job-owned".to_string(),
+                ))
+            })?;
+            if owner.job.job_id.as_ref() != record.job_id {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated child Plan changed Job owner".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+            validate_owned_plan_if_present(paths, plan_id, &record.job_id)?;
+            if record.immutable_plan_sha256.as_deref()
+                != Some(immutable_plan_sha256(&plan)?.as_str())
+            {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated child Plan definition changed after approval".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+            let task = plan.tasks.get(*task_index as usize).ok_or_else(|| {
+                CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated child task index is absent".to_string(),
+                ))
+            })?;
+            if task.task_id != *task_id
+                || task.status != deadreckon_core::PlanTaskStatus::Running
+                || task.attempts.len() as u32 + 1 != *task_attempt
+            {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated child does not match the exact running task attempt".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+            let expected_scope = canonical_invocation_path(
+                &paths.plan_dir(plan_id).join("launch").join(task_id),
+                "task launch scope",
+            )?;
+            if expected_scope != record.scope_root {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated child scope does not match its exact Plan task".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+        }
+        DelegatedAction::PlanFork { plan_id } | DelegatedAction::PlanMerge { plan_id } => {
+            let plan = deadreckon_core::load_plan(paths, plan_id)?;
+            let owner = resolve_plan_owner(paths, &plan)?.ok_or_else(|| {
+                CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated Plan operation is no longer Job-owned".to_string(),
+                ))
+            })?;
+            if owner.job.job_id.as_ref() != record.job_id {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated Plan operation changed Job owner".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+            validate_owned_plan_if_present(paths, plan_id, &record.job_id)?;
+            if record.immutable_plan_sha256.as_deref()
+                != Some(immutable_plan_sha256(&plan)?.as_str())
+            {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated Plan definition changed after approval".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+        }
+        DelegatedAction::CampaignSub {
+            campaign_id,
+            sub_id,
+        } => {
+            if campaign_id != &record.job_id {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated campaign does not match its durable Job".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+            let campaign =
+                deadreckon_core::campaign::read_campaign(&paths.plan_dir(campaign_id))?;
+            if !campaign.sub_goals.iter().any(|sub| sub.sub_id == *sub_id) {
+                return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                    "delegated campaign sub-goal is absent from the approved schedule".to_string(),
+                )));
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}

+pub(crate) fn authorize_delegated_invocation_if_present() -> Result<bool> {

+            "delegated invocation record exceeded its bounded size".to_string(),

+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "delegated invocation token exceeded its bounded size".to_string(),
+        )));

+    let token = std::str::from_utf8(&token_bytes)

+        )));
+    }
+    if !commands::supervisor::guarded_driver_authority_is_live(&paths, &record.authority)? {

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 02:27:54Z)**_

From the beginning of this loop, we have built most of the durable execution foundation. We have not yet proved the entire product promise in real-world use.

## Implemented and committed locally

Nine commits are currently on local `main`, ahead of `origin/main`.

### Durable Jobs

- A durable `Job`, event-history and lease protocol.
- Append-only lifecycle events as the source of operational truth.
- Detached execution supervised outside the initiating terminal.
- Renewable, fenced leases with stale-lease reclamation.
- Bounded retry, spend and time policies.
- Explicit terminal outcomes including verified, blocked, cancelled, failed and budget-exhausted.
- Recovery after supervisor and worker interruption.
- Crash-atomic worker launch: a worker cannot begin mutating state until its launch has been durably recorded.
- Single runs, Graph plans and Campaigns entering the durable scheduler.

### Independent verification

Completion now requires two keys:

1. Deterministic acceptance checks pass.
2. A fresh, read-only semantic judge assesses the goal, contract, result, diff and evidence.

The semantic judge can return achieved, revise or uncertain. It cannot override failed deterministic checks. A required judge being unavailable cannot silently produce success.

### Trusted receipts and gate protection

- HMAC-SHA-256 receipts.
- Signing material kept outside the agent workspace.
- Receipt binding to the goal contract, acceptance result, semantic judgment, source/result revisions and result-tree digest.
- Frozen authority and proof paths.
- Revalidation before promotion or `finish`.
- Synthetic or agent-authored completion evidence is rejected.
- Tampered or missing receipts fail closed.
- Tests exercise trust-boundary attacks and crash positions.

### Operator surface and documentation

The durable workflow is shaped around:

- `start`
- `attach`
- `status`
- `list`
- `finish`
- cancellation and supervisor recovery

There is also an extensive manual acceptance script covering detachment, lease recovery, worker death, semantic judging and receipt tampering: [WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md).

### Dogfood infrastructure

- A 24-scenario trial matrix.
- Metrics for verified completion, intervention, recovery, judging, tampering and receipt validation.
- Credential-free adversarial scenarios.
- Tests ensuring the harness derives results from durable evidence rather than trusting its own narration.

The committed baseline passed `make verify`.

## Implemented but not yet committed

The current checkpoint closes a subtle but important hole: nested work must remain subordinate to one root Job.

It currently adds:

- Explicit `owner_job_id` ownership for every Plan.
- Verified parent/child Plan lineage.
- Protected immutable definitions for every owned Plan.
- Refusal of public `fork`, `merge` and hidden driver routes when a Plan belongs to a durable Job.
- Private authentication for the root Graph/Campaign driver.
- One-use delegated capabilities for:
  - Plan children
  - nested Plan forks
  - nested Plan merges
  - Campaign sub-plans
- Capabilities bound to the exact Job, lease, attempt, command arguments, working directory, scope and Plan definition.
- Tokens delivered through private stdin rather than predictable environment variables.
- Atomic consumption so a delegated invocation cannot be replayed.
- Cancelling a nested Plan routes to its root Job.

The focused root-Graph, spoofing and ownership tests are passing. The new nested-Plan end-to-end test currently has a test-harness failure: replay `start` does not emit the JSON the test attempted to parse. That checkpoint is therefore not yet ready to commit, even though the underlying nested execution has not been shown to be the failure.

## Still on the docket

### 1. Finish and land nested ownership

- Fix the nested test harness.
- Prove a nested Plan creates exactly one Job.
- Add replay, wrong-token, wrong-command, wrong-directory and stale-lease tests.
- Re-run restart and trust-boundary suites.
- Run full `make verify`.
- Commit the checkpoint locally.

### 2. Close the remaining Chain boundary

Chain still has some legacy lifecycle behavior:

- Reject unsupported durable Chain policy before spending money on planning.
- Remove old operator suggestions to use legacy `chain run` or `chain resume`.
- Replace an environment-variable debug escape with a dedicated test-only characterization route.
- Ensure Chain execution cannot bypass the Job scheduler.

### 3. Complete product consolidation

The underlying model is converging, but the code still visibly contains Runs, Plans, Chains, Campaigns and Jobs. We need to finish making those execution shapes subordinate implementations of one Job lifecycle, then simplify the normal CLI and documentation accordingly.

### 4. Perform real adversarial dogfooding

This is the largest unfinished proof.

The current 24-task matrix has only two fully attempted trials. Credential-free testing has seven passes and five still unproven. We still need to:

- Run 20–30 real tasks across repositories and providers.
- Kill terminals, workers and supervisors.
- Exercise restart-at-login or machine-restart recovery.
- Remove network access during execution.
- Tamper with gates, receipts and protected paths.
- Run DeadReckon on DeadReckon.
- Measure false acceptance, false rejection, recovery, intervention, comprehension time and cost.

## Honest overall assessment

The durable Single-Job system and two-key verification model are real and committed. Graphs and Campaigns now enter that model, but nested execution is still being secured so it cannot escape or manufacture additional Jobs. Chain remains the principal legacy boundary. The dogfood framework exists, but the evidence volume is not yet sufficient to claim the final promise.

In rough terms:

- Durable execution foundation: largely complete.
- Semantic verification and trusted receipt: largely complete.
- One-Job ownership across nested execution: close, currently uncommitted.
- Chain convergence: unfinished.
- Real-world proof and product simplification: substantially unfinished.

Also, none of these nine commits has been pushed: local `main` is nine commits ahead of `origin/main`, and the current ownership checkpoint is still uncommitted.

+        "n": campaign.n,
+        "depth": campaign.depth,

+fn owned_campaign_record_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> PathBuf {

+
+pub(crate) fn record_owned_campaign(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    campaign: &deadreckon_core::campaign::Campaign,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let Some(context) = DRIVER_CONTEXT.get() else {
+        return Ok(());
+    };
+    if context.job_id != campaign.campaign_id {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "Campaign {} does not retain current durable Job identity {}",
+            campaign.campaign_id, context.job_id
+        ))));
+    }
+    let job = deadreckon_core::load_job(paths, &context.job_id)?;
+    if job.shape != JobShape::LegacyCampaign {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "Campaign {} belongs to incompatible durable Job shape {:?}",
+            campaign.campaign_id, job.shape
+        ))));
+    }
+    if !commands::supervisor::guarded_driver_authority_is_live(paths, &context.authority)? {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "Campaign definition cannot be frozen without current fenced authority".to_string(),
+        )));
+    }
+    let record = OwnedCampaignRecord {
+        schema_version: 1,
+        job_id: context.job_id.clone(),
+        immutable_definition_sha256: immutable_campaign_sha256(campaign)?,
+        recorded_at: Utc::now(),
+    };
+    let path = owned_campaign_record_path(paths, &context.job_id);
+    if path.is_file() {
+        let existing: OwnedCampaignRecord = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path)?)?;
+        if existing.schema_version != 1
+            || existing.job_id != record.job_id
+            || existing.immutable_definition_sha256 != record.immutable_definition_sha256
+        {
+            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                "Campaign no longer matches its protected Job-owned definition".to_string(),
+            )));
+        }
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    commands::job::write_json_synced(&path, &record)
+}
+
+fn validate_owned_campaign(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    campaign: &deadreckon_core::campaign::Campaign,
+    job_id: &str,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    if campaign.campaign_id != job_id {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "Campaign changed its durable Job identity".to_string(),
+        )));
+    }
+    let path = owned_campaign_record_path(paths, job_id);
+    let record: OwnedCampaignRecord = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path).map_err(|source| {
+        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::Io {
+            path: path.clone(),
+            source,
+        })
+    })?)?;
+    if record.schema_version != 1
+        || record.job_id != job_id
+        || record.immutable_definition_sha256 != immutable_campaign_sha256(campaign)?
+    {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "Campaign no longer matches its protected Job-owned definition".to_string(),
+        )));
+    }

+                "delegated invocation argument is too large to hash".to_string(),
+            ))
+        })?;
+        hasher.update(length.to_le_bytes());
+        hasher.update(bytes);
+    }
+    Ok(format!("sha256:{:x}", hasher.finalize()))

+        parts.push(format!("--model {}", quote_chain_goal_arg(model)));

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 04:35:09Z)**_

The core promise now exists, but the loop is not finished. We have a durable, independently verified Job system; the remaining work is integration hardening, cross-platform proof, and real-world dogfooding.

## Already implemented and committed

Nine commits are on local `main`, which is currently nine commits ahead of `origin/main`.

### Durable Job execution

- `deadreckon start` creates a durable Job and hands it to a detached supervisor.
- Jobs have append-only event histories, leases, heartbeats and recoverable projections.
- Abandoned work can be reclaimed after process failure.
- Child launch is crash-atomic: recovery can distinguish “prepared”, “released” and “actually running”.
- Retry, time and spend policies are persisted.
- Terminal outcomes distinguish verified, needs review, cancelled, failed and exhausted conditions.
- `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list` and `finish` operate around the Job abstraction.
- Run, Plan, Campaign and compatible Chain execution have been routed toward Jobs.

### Two-key completion

Completion now requires both:

1. Deterministic acceptance checks.
2. An independent semantic judgment.

The semantic judge returns achieved, revise or uncertain. Uncertain or unavailable strict judging becomes `NEEDS REVIEW`; it cannot override failed deterministic checks.

Synthetic or agent-authored completion evidence is rejected.

### Signed verification receipts

- Gate and receipt signing use HMAC-SHA-256.
- Signing material is stored outside the agent workspace.
- Receipts bind the approved authority, contract, launch plan, deterministic marker, semantic judgment, source revision, result revision and result tree.
- A modified result or judgment invalidates the receipt.
- `finish` accepts only a valid combined receipt.
- Provider and sandbox boundaries include protected-path controls and adversarial tests.

### Operator-facing documentation

The operator contract, architecture, concepts, schemas, acceptance checklist and `MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md` were updated to describe this model.

### Initial dogfood machinery

There is now:

- a trial matrix;
- metrics collection;
- adversarial tampering scenarios;
- credential-free test results;
- crash and restart tests;
- tests for forged or synthetic completion evidence.

The committed baseline passed `make verify`.

## Implemented in the working tree, but not committed yet

This is the large hardening tranche produced after the subagent audits.

- Plans now record their owning Job.
- Nested Plans remain under one root Job instead of creating additional Jobs.
- Public `fork`, `merge`, repair and kill routes are fenced when a Job owns the Plan.
- Approved Plan definitions are frozen and checked across the complete parent/child lineage.
- Cycles, broken parent links and excessive nesting fail closed.
- Nested Plan recovery handles a crash after the child merged but before the parent recorded the result.
- Campaign schedules are frozen and cryptographically bound to delegated work.
- Delegated child capabilities bind the exact Job, action, arguments, directory, schedule and live lease.
- Capabilities are one-use and revoked on launch failure.
- Plaintext launch secrets were removed from persisted acknowledgements; descendants no longer inherit supervisor authentication variables.
- Delegation persistence received Unix directory syncing and non-UTF-8 argument support.
- Chain requests are being preflighted before paying a planner for a configuration that cannot execute.
- Chain status/help is being changed so it recommends durable migration or inspection instead of legacy `chain run` and `chain resume`.

Most focused ownership, Campaign, restart and trust tests passed before the latest packaging change.

## What is immediately unfinished

The current working tree is not ready to commit. Today’s check exposed a half-completed Cargo configuration change for the separate legacy-characterization binary: the ordinary `deadreckon` binary target is no longer visible to integration tests.

That needs to be corrected before anything else. The old debug environment-variable escape also still appears in the Plan, Chain and Orchestrate test paths, so the safe test-only binary transition is incomplete.

Then we need to:

- update the Chain and Orchestrate characterization tests;
- add “no provider spend before refusal” tests;
- prove `--draft` remains inert;
- prove the old environment variable cannot unlock product execution;
- update Makefile and CI feature selection;
- run debug and release test profiles;
- run the complete verification suite;
- perform the operator acceptance checklist;
- commit this tranche to local `main`.

## Still on the larger docket

### One Job model

We have converged much of execution, but legacy Chain lifecycle code and duplicated status concepts still exist. We need to finish making Chains and Plans scheduling shapes over Jobs, with Job history as the authoritative lifecycle record.

### Durability cleanup

- Bound or prune consumed delegation records.
- Sweep capabilities from stale lease epochs and terminal Jobs.
- Prove directory syncing and process recovery on Linux and Windows.
- Exercise actual machine/service restart, not only controlled process crashes.

### Trust-boundary closure

The important mechanisms are present, but the current uncommitted ownership and capability work must be integrated and tested across every provider/tool route.

### Real dogfooding

The harness exists; the requested 20–30 real tasks do not yet.

We still need to run multiple repositories and providers while deliberately:

- killing the CLI, worker and supervisor;
- restarting the machine or service;
- removing network access;
- tampering with gates and receipts;
- modifying scheduled Plan/Campaign definitions;
- running DeadReckon on DeadReckon.

We then need to report verified completion rate, recovery rate, false acceptance/rejection, intervention count, comprehension time and judging cost.

## Bottom line

We have moved from “a design for durable goal execution” to “a functioning durable Job engine with two-key verification and signed receipts.”

We have not yet reached the final claim because the newest ownership/security tranche is uncommitted and temporarily fails compilation, cross-platform recovery remains under-proven, and the full live dogfood campaign has not happened. Also, none of the nine completed commits have been pushed to `origin/main`; they currently exist only on the local `main`.

+async fn product_chain_plan_refuses_unsupported_policy_before_provider_spend() {
+    let cases: &[&[&str]] = &[
+        &["--n", "7"],
+        &["--apply-mode", "manual"],
+        &["--sandbox", "none"],
+    ];
+
+    for extra_args in cases {
+        let temp = repo_tempdir();
+        let repo = clean_git_repo(&temp);
+        let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
+        let server = MockServer::start(r#"["one","two"]"#).await;
+        write_config(temp.path(), &server.base_url());
+        let mut command = base_deadreckon(&paths);
+        command
+            .current_dir(&repo)
+            .args(["chain", "plan", "build thing", "--provider", "mock"])
+            .args(*extra_args);
+
+        let output = command.output().expect("product chain plan preflight");
+
+        assert!(!output.status.success());
+        let stderr = stderr(&output);
+        assert!(stderr.contains("planner spend"), "{stderr}");
+        assert!(stderr.contains("$0.00"), "{stderr}");
+        assert!(server.journal().is_empty(), "{:?}", server.journal());
+        assert!(
+            !paths.chains_dir().exists()
+                || fs::read_dir(paths.chains_dir())
+                    .expect("chains")
+                    .next()
+                    .is_none()
+        );
+        assert!(
+            !paths.jobs_dir().exists()
+                || fs::read_dir(paths.jobs_dir())
+                    .expect("jobs")
+                    .next()
+                    .is_none()
+        );
+    }
+}

+        ])

+        .expect("product chain draft");
+
+    assert_success(&output);
+    assert_eq!(server.journal().len(), 1);
+    let chain = newest_chain(&paths);

+    assert!(chain.steps.iter().all(|step| step.run_id.is_none()));
+    assert!(!paths.conductor_json(&chain.chain_id).exists());
+    assert!(
+        !paths.jobs_dir().exists()
+            || fs::read_dir(paths.jobs_dir())
+                .expect("jobs")
+                .next()
+                .is_none()
+    );
+}

+        fs::write(&pending, b"replayed protected record").expect("replayed pending record");
+        let error =
+            claim_delegation_record(&pending, &consumed, b"replayed protected record")
+                .expect_err("consumed tombstone must fail closed");
+        assert!(error.to_string().contains("already consumed"), "{error}");
+        assert!(
+            pending.exists(),
+            "the replay record remains available for recovery diagnostics"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            fs::read(&consumed).expect("original tombstone"),
+            b"first protected record",
+            "a replay must not replace the original consumed evidence"
+        );
+    }

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 05:52:23Z)**_

The core DeadReckon promise is largely implemented in code. What remains is mainly integration, live proof, cross-platform hardening, and simplification.

## Implemented and committed locally

Nine commits are on local `main`, covering:

| Original objective | Current achievement |
|---|---|
| Durable goal executor | Jobs have durable IDs, append-only lifecycle events, detached supervision, fenced leases, retries, cancellation, typed stop reasons and persisted recovery state. |
| Two-key completion | Deterministic checks must pass before a fresh, read-only semantic judge can accept the result. A failed check cannot be overridden by the judge. |
| Tamper-resistant gate | HMAC-SHA-256 receipts, external signing keys, protected control paths, containment evidence and result-tree digests are implemented. |
| One job model | Direct runs, orchestration, supported chains and campaigns now create Single, Graph or Campaign Jobs under the same supervisor and receipt boundary. |
| Clear operator lifecycle | `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list`, `cancel` and `finish` operate on durable Job state. |
| Isolation and promotion | Work runs in isolated codebases and is only promoted after the receipt is revalidated. |
| Evidence and reporting | Jobs retain authority, contracts, events, checks, semantic judgment, revisions, spend information and a final completion receipt. |
| Test infrastructure | Fault, restart, trust-boundary, receipt-forgery and credential-free adversarial tests exist. A 24-case live dogfood kit also exists. |

The architectural centre is described in [MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md:78). Job creation lives in [job.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/job.rs:57), while shared Graph/Campaign verification is in [graph_job.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/graph_job.rs:1455).

These nine commits represent roughly 30,000 added lines across 118 files. They are on local `main`, which is nine commits ahead of `origin/main`. They have not been pushed.

## Implemented but not yet committed

The current working tranche adds another substantial hardening layer:

- Plan and Campaign artifacts are bound to their owning Job.
- Delegated child capabilities are single-use and restricted to the exact Job, action, arguments, directory and active lease.
- Campaign child Plan IDs are reserved before launch, so a crash cannot produce an unidentified or duplicated child.
- Campaigns can recover the same child across four tested crash windows.
- Nested Plan lineage is frozen and validated.
- Protected credentials are removed from descendant environments.
- Chain policy is checked before spending provider calls.
- Unsupported Chain execution fails before creating state.
- Historical Chain execution is isolated in a feature-gated characterization binary and cannot be unlocked through an environment variable in the production CLI.
- CI, release and Makefile coverage now test both the production and characterization boundaries.

Focused verification is strong:

- Chain: 131 tests passing in debug and release.
- Orchestration: 180 tests passing in debug and release.
- Campaign: 75 unit tests and 7 integration tests passing.
- Job ownership: 8 tests passing.
- Restart and trust-boundary suites passing.
- Four Campaign crash windows passing.

This tranche is roughly 2,500 additional lines. It still needs final repository-wide verification and a local commit.

## Still on the docket

Immediate integration work:

1. Fix one small new Clippy warning.
2. Run formatting, metadata and scoped whitespace checks.
3. Run the complete `make verify`.
4. Review the exact patch for accidental compatibility leaks.
5. Produce the operator acceptance checklist.
6. Commit the tranche to local `main`.
7. Push only when you explicitly authorize it.

Product-proof work:

- Run the 24-case live dogfood matrix. At present, only 2 live cases have been attempted; 22 remain.
- Test multiple real repositories and providers.
- Kill workers and supervisors during actual work.
- Reboot the machine during a Job.
- Remove network access during execution.
- Attempt live gate and receipt tampering.
- Measure false acceptance, false rejection, recovery rate, interventions, cost and comprehension time.
- Establish Linux and Windows parity; current strongest crash testing is on macOS.
- Close or explicitly document the Windows directory-durability gap.

Remaining product/architecture decisions:

- Add safe Graph and Campaign repair after the semantic judge returns `revise`.
- Retire or preserve the remaining historical Chain, preview and uncontained compatibility modes.
- Finish structured-event, usage-accounting and steering parity across providers.
- Simplify overlapping narration and advanced orchestration surfaces.
- Keep deeper Campaign, learning and self-improvement expansion frozen until dogfooding proves they are useful.
- Eventually add rules-as-gate and MCP access, after the core execution promise is demonstrated.

## Bottom line

We have built the machinery needed for this statement:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive process interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify checks and meaning, and leave a tamper-resistant receipt.

What we have not yet earned is the word “reliably” across real machines, providers and failure conditions. The next milestone is therefore not another large feature tranche. It is: finish and commit the current hardening work, then run the live adversarial dogfood programme and fix only failures revealed by that evidence.

fn durable_chain_start_command(chain: &Chain) -> String {
    let mut parts = vec!["deadreckon chain --yes".to_string()];
    if let Some(provider) = chain.provider.as_deref() {
        parts.push(format!("--provider {}", quote_chain_goal_arg(provider)));
    }
    if let Some(model) = chain.model.as_deref() {
        parts.push(format!("--model {}", quote_chain_goal_arg(model)));
    }
    if chain.sandbox != "auto" && chain.sandbox != "none" {
        parts.push(format!(
            "--sandbox {}",
            quote_chain_goal_arg(&chain.sandbox)
        ));
    }
    if let Some(max_spend) = chain.max_spend_usd {
        parts.push(format!("--max-spend {max_spend:.6}"));
    }
    if let Some(max_wall) = chain.max_wall_seconds {
        parts.push(format!("--max-wall-seconds {max_wall:.3}"));
    }
    parts.extend(
        chain
            .steps
            .iter()
            .map(|step| quote_chain_goal_arg(&step.goal)),
    );
    parts.join(" ")
}

fn durable_chain_migration_command(chain: &Chain) -> String {
    if chain.steps.len() <= 6 {
        return durable_chain_start_command(chain);
    }
    let ordered_goal = ordered_chain_goal(
        &chain
            .steps
            .iter()
            .map(|step| step.goal.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    let mut parts = vec![
        "deadreckon start".to_string(),
        quote_chain_goal_arg(&ordered_goal),
        "--mode full-plan".to_string(),
        "--children 6".to_string(),
        "--yes".to_string(),
    ];
    if let Some(provider) = chain.provider.as_deref() {
        parts.push(format!("--provider {}", quote_chain_goal_arg(provider)));
    }
    if let Some(model) = chain.model.as_deref() {
        parts.push(format!("--model {}", quote_chain_goal_arg(model)));
    }
    parts.join(" ")
}

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn unsupported_durable_chain_policy(
    step_count: usize,
    branch_policy: BranchPolicy,
    apply_mode: ApplyMode,
    apply_strategy: ApplyStrategy,
    apply_allowlist: &[String],
    on_fail: OnFail,
    circuit_breaker_threshold: u32,
    sandbox: &str,
    requested_base: Option<&str>,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut unsupported = Vec::new();
    if step_count > 6 {
        unsupported.push(format!(
            "{step_count} steps (durable linear jobs currently support at most 6)"
        ));
    }
    if branch_policy != BranchPolicy::Stack {
        // The rich glyph stays Unicode when not plain.
        assert!(!chain_step_glyph(ChainStepStatus::Pending, false).is_ascii());
    }
}

fn print_chain_paused_footer(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, chain: &Chain) {
    print!(
        "{}",
        chain_verdict_surface(paths, chain).render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false))
    );
}

fn deadreckon(paths: &DeadreckonPaths) -> Command {
    let mut command = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_deadreckon"));
    command
        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", paths.home())
        .env("NO_COLOR", "1")
        .env("COLUMNS", "120")
        .env("RUST_BACKTRACE", "0")
        .env_remove("DEADRECKON_CAMPAIGN_DEPTH")
        .env_remove("DEADRECKON_CAMPAIGN_ROOT")
        .env_remove("DEADRECKON_CAMPAIGN_ANCESTOR_TASK_KEYS")
        .env_remove("DEADRECKON_CAMPAIGN_ANCESTOR_SCOPES")
        .env_remove("DEADRECKON_CAMPAIGN_SUB_RESULT");
    command
}

fn kv_value_width(prefix_width: usize) -> usize {
    let terminal_width = crossterm::terminal::size()
        .ok()
        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
        .or_else(|| {
            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
                .ok()
                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
        })
        .filter(|columns| *columns > 1)
        .unwrap_or(120)
        .saturating_sub(1);
    terminal_width.saturating_sub(prefix_width).max(20)
}

fn wrap_kv_value(value: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {

}

}

fn merge_stop_reason(reason: StopReason, extra: Value) -> Value {
    let mut detail = match extra {
        Value::Object(detail) => detail,
        Value::Null => serde_json::Map::new(),
        value => {
            let mut detail = serde_json::Map::new();
            detail.insert("detail".to_string(), value);
            detail
        }
    };
    detail.insert(
        "stop_reason".to_string(),
        serde_json::to_value(reason).unwrap_or(Value::String("corrupt_history".to_string())),
    );
    Value::Object(detail)
}

fn boot_identity() -> String {
    if let Some(value) = std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_BOOT_ID")
        && !value.is_empty()
    {
        return value.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    if let Ok(value) = fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id") {
        let value = value.trim();
        if !value.is_empty() {
            return value.to_string();
        }
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    if let Ok(output) = Command::new("sysctl")
        .args(["-n", "kern.boottime"])
        .output()
        && output.status.success()
    {
        let value = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
        let value = value.trim();
        if !value.is_empty() {
            return format!("macos:{value}");
        }
    }
    // Unknown is deliberately stable. A random per-process value would look
    // like a reboot and could reclaim a live lease; stable unknown instead
    // waits for normal expiry and fails safely.
    "unknown-boot".to_string()
}

    {

        let command_end = raw.rfind(')')?;
        let fields = raw[command_end + 1..]
            .split_whitespace()
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();

pub(crate) fn require_current_driver_for_job_artifact(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    artifact_id: &str,
    expected_shape: JobShape,
    operation: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    let owner = if expected_shape == JobShape::Graph {
        let plan = deadreckon_core::load_plan(paths, artifact_id)?;
        resolve_plan_owner(paths, &plan)?
    } else if paths.job_json(artifact_id).is_file() {
        let job = deadreckon_core::load_job(paths, artifact_id)?;
        if job.job_id.as_ref() != artifact_id || job.shape != expected_shape {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
                "{operation} found artifact {artifact_id} colliding with incompatible durable Job {}",
                job.job_id
            ))));
        }
        Some(ResolvedPlanOwner {
            root_plan_id: artifact_id.to_string(),
            lineage: vec![artifact_id.to_string()],
            job,
        })
    } else {
        None
    };
    let Some(owner) = owner else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    if owner.root_plan_id.trim().is_empty() || owner.lineage.is_empty() {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "{operation} found incomplete durable Plan ownership for {artifact_id}"
        ))));
    }
    if let Some(context) = DRIVER_CONTEXT
        .get()
        .filter(|context| context.job_id == owner.job.job_id.as_ref())
    {
        if context.authority.job_id != owner.job.job_id.as_ref()
            || !commands::supervisor::guarded_driver_authority_is_live(paths, &context.authority)?
        {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
                "{operation} refused stale authority for durable Job {}",
                owner.job.job_id
            ))));
        }
        validate_owned_plan_lineage(paths, &owner)?;
        return Ok(());
    }
    Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
        &format!(
            "{operation} cannot mutate {} because it belongs to durable Job {}",
            run_prefix(artifact_id),
            run_prefix(owner.job.job_id.as_ref())
        ),
        &format!(
            "deadreckon attach {}",
            run_prefix(owner.job.job_id.as_ref())
        ),
    )))
}

pub(crate) fn record_current_artifact(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    kind: DriverKind,
    artifact_kind: &str,
    artifact_id: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    let Some(context) = DRIVER_CONTEXT.get() else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    if !context.root_artifact {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let job_id = context.job_id.as_str();
    if job_id != artifact_id {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "advanced driver artifact {artifact_id} does not retain parent job identity {job_id}"
        ))));
    }
    let state = DriverState {
        schema_version: 1,
        job_id: JobId(job_id.to_string()),
        kind,
        artifact_kind: artifact_kind.to_string(),
        artifact_id: artifact_id.to_string(),
        recorded_at: Utc::now(),
    };
    let path = driver_state_path(paths, job_id);
    if path.exists() {
        let existing = load_driver_state(paths, job_id)?;
        if existing.job_id != state.job_id
            || existing.kind != state.kind
            || existing.artifact_kind != state.artifact_kind
            || existing.artifact_id != state.artifact_id
        {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
                "advanced artifact mapping for job {job_id} changed across attempts"
            ))));
        }
        return Ok(());
    }
    commands::job::write_json_synced(&path, &state)?;
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) async fn drive_job_command(job_id: String) -> Result<()> {
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
    let authority = commands::supervisor::require_guarded_driver_launch(&paths, &job_id)?;
    let job = deadreckon_core::load_job(&paths, &job_id)?;
    if job.job_id.as_ref() != job_id {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "advanced driver job identity mismatch".to_string(),
        )));
    }
    let plan = commands::course::load_launch_plan(&paths.job_launch_plan(&job_id))?;
    let driver = driver_spec(&plan)?;
    install_driver_context(&paths, authority, true)?;
    std::env::set_current_dir(&job.source_cwd)?;

    match driver.kind {
        DriverKind::Review | DriverKind::FullPlan => {
            if job.shape != JobShape::Graph {
                return Err(driver_shape_error(&job_id));
            }
            drive_plan(&paths, &job, plan, driver).await
        }
        DriverKind::Campaign => {
            if job.shape != JobShape::LegacyCampaign {
                return Err(driver_shape_error(&job_id));
            }
            drive_campaign(&paths, &job, driver).await
        }
    }
}

/// Append one control fact while holding the per-job lock, then checkpoint the
/// projection. The event is durable before the projection it authorizes.
pub fn append_job_event(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, event: &JobEvent) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    fs::create_dir_all(paths.job_dir(event.job_id.as_ref()))
        .with_path(paths.job_dir(event.job_id.as_ref()))?;
    let lock_path = paths.job_dir(event.job_id.as_ref()).join(JOB_CONTROL_LOCK);
    let lock = open_job_control_lock(&lock_path)?;
    lock.lock_exclusive().with_path(&lock_path)?;
    append_job_event_locked(paths, event)
}

/// Append while the caller holds this job's control lock. Lease operations
/// use this seam so ownership validation and the authorized event are one
/// serialized transaction.
pub(crate) fn append_job_event_locked(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    event: &JobEvent,
) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let events_path = paths.job_events(event.job_id.as_ref());
    let history = read_job_history(&events_path)?;
    if !history.caveats.is_empty() {
        return Err(history_corrupt(
            event.job_id.as_ref(),
            "cannot append after a torn final event row",
        ));
    }
    for (existing, raw) in history.events.iter().zip(&history.raw_lines) {
        if existing.event_id != event.event_id {
            continue;
        }
        let candidate = serde_json::to_vec(event).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
            path: events_path.clone(),
            source,
        })?;
        if candidate == *raw {
            return reduce_job_history(&event.job_id, &history);
        }
        return Err(history_corrupt(
            event.job_id.as_ref(),
            &format!(
                "event id {} already exists with different bytes",
                event.event_id
            ),
        ));
    }
    let expected = history
        .events
        .last()
        .map_or(1, |prior| prior.sequence.get() + 1);
    if event.sequence.get() != expected {
        return Err(history_corrupt(
            event.job_id.as_ref(),
            &format!(
                "append expected sequence {expected}, received {}",
                event.sequence.get()
            ),
        ));
    }

    append_synced_json_line(&events_path, event)?;
    let rebuilt = read_job_history(&events_path)?;
    let projection = reduce_job_history(&event.job_id, &rebuilt)?;
    atomic_write_json(&paths.job_projection(event.job_id.as_ref()), &projection)?;
    Ok(projection)
}

pub fn rebuild_job_projection(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let job = load_job(paths, job_id)?;
    let history = read_job_history(&paths.job_events(job_id))?;
    let projection = reduce_job_history(&job.job_id, &history)?;
    atomic_write_json(&paths.job_projection(job_id), &projection)?;
    Ok(projection)
}

pub fn load_job_projection(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let path = paths.job_projection(job_id);
    let raw = fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(path)
}

    OpenOptions::new()
        .create(true)
        .read(true)
        .write(true)
        .truncate(false)
        .open(path)
        .with_path(path)
}

/// Renew the current lease without changing execution phase or event history.
pub fn heartbeat_job_lease(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
    ttl: Duration,
) -> Result<JobLease> {
    let expires_at = lease_expiry(now, ttl)?;
    let lock_path = paths.job_dir(token.job_id.as_ref()).join(JOB_CONTROL_LOCK);
    let lock = open_job_control_lock(&lock_path)?;
    FileExt::lock_exclusive(&lock).with_path(&lock_path)?;

    let mut lease = load_job_lease(paths, &token.job_id)?;
    validate_token(&lease, token, now)?;
    lease.heartbeat_at = now;
    lease.expires_at = expires_at;
    atomic_write_json(&paths.job_lease(token.job_id.as_ref()), &lease)?;
    Ok(lease)
}

/// Append one worker lifecycle fact only when its lease epoch is still current.
pub fn append_fenced_job_event(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
    event: &JobEvent,
) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let lock_path = paths.job_dir(token.job_id.as_ref()).join(JOB_CONTROL_LOCK);
    let lock = open_job_control_lock(&lock_path)?;
    FileExt::lock_exclusive(&lock).with_path(&lock_path)?;

    let lease = load_job_lease(paths, &token.job_id)?;
    validate_token(&lease, token, now)?;
    if event.job_id != token.job_id {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!("event belongs to {}", event.job_id),
        ));
    }
    if event.lease_epoch != token.epoch {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!(
                "event lease epoch {} does not match token epoch {}",
                event.lease_epoch, token.epoch
            ),
        ));
    }
    append_job_event_locked(paths, event)
}

        JobShape::Single => CourseShape::Single,
        JobShape::Graph => CourseShape::Plan,
        JobShape::LegacyCampaign => CourseShape::Campaign,
        JobShape::LegacyChain => CourseShape::ChainExtend,
    };
    if plan.shape != expected_shape || plan.goal != job.goal {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "launch plan identity does not match job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    if job.shape != JobShape::Single {
        super::graph_job::driver_spec(&plan)?;
    }

    let authority_path = paths.job_authority(job.job_id.as_ref());
    let authority_digest = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&authority_path)?;
    if authority_digest != job.authority_sha256 {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "authority digest mismatch for job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    let authority: JobAuthority = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&authority_path)?)?;
    if authority.job_id != job.job_id
        || authority.run_id != RunId(job.job_id.as_ref().to_string())
        || authority.launch_plan_sha256 != job.launch_plan_sha256
    {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "authority identity does not match job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "goal",
        &authority.goal_sha256,
        &deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(&job.goal),
    )?;
    let contract_path = super::job::job_acceptance_path(paths, job.job_id.as_ref());
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "done contract",
        &authority.contract_sha256,
        &deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&contract_path)?,
    )?;
    let policy_sha256 = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(
        &serde_json::to_string(&job.policy).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
            path: paths.job_json(job.job_id.as_ref()),
            source,
        })?,
    );
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "effective policy",
        &authority.effective_policy_sha256,
        &policy_sha256,
    )?;
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "source tree",
        &authority.source_tree_sha256,
        &deadreckon_core::flight::build_working_file_index(&job.source_cwd)?.tree_hash(),
    )?;
    if authority.semantic_judge_mode != job.policy.semantic_judge {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "semantic judge policy mismatch for job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    if let Some(expected) = authority.source_revision.as_deref()
        && current_source_revision(&job.source_cwd).as_deref() != Some(expected)
    {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "source revision changed after job {} was approved",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    Ok(LaunchInputs { plan, authority })
}

pub(crate) fn write_json_synced<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "job artifact path has no parent: {}",
            path.display()
        )))
    })?;
    fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
    let mut file = OpenOptions::new().create_new(true).write(true).open(path)?;
    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut file, value).map_err(|source| {
        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::Json {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            source,
        })
    })?;
    file.write_all(b"\n")?;
    file.sync_all()?;
    #[cfg(unix)]
    fs::File::open(parent)?.sync_all()?;
    Ok(())
}

fn sync_file(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    fs::File::open(path)?.sync_all()?;
    Ok(())
}

) -> Option<StopReason> {
    match decision {

        Some(SemanticDecision::Achieved) | None => None,
    }

pub(crate) fn embed_driver_spec(
    plan: &mut commands::course::LaunchPlan,
    driver: &DriverSpec,
) -> Result<()> {
    let mut driver = driver.clone();
    if matches!(
        driver.kind,
        DriverKind::Review | DriverKind::FullPlan | DriverKind::Campaign
    ) {
        // A PerNode plan mutates the approved source while the durable parent
        // is still being verified. Strict Graph Jobs therefore always merge
        // in isolation and expose one receipt-bound parent result at the end.
        driver.apply = deadreckon_core::plan::ApplyWhen::AtEnd;
    }
    let mut signals = plan.signals.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    signals.insert(DRIVER_SIGNAL.to_string(), serde_json::to_value(&driver)?);
    plan.signals = serde_json::Value::Object(signals);
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn driver_spec(plan: &commands::course::LaunchPlan) -> Result<DriverSpec> {
    let value = plan.signals.get(DRIVER_SIGNAL).ok_or_else(|| {
        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "advanced job launch plan is missing its immutable driver specification".to_string(),
        ))
    })?;
    serde_json::from_value(value.clone()).map_err(CliError::from)
}

) -> Result<()> {
    let record = PlanPlannerAccounting {

    super::job::write_json_synced(

    )

/// Create a child plan for every seeded node that carries its own graph, and
/// link it by id.
///
/// Runs after the parent exists because the link is bidirectional: the child
/// records `parent_plan_id` (which bounds nesting depth) and the parent's task
/// records `subplan`. A child that cannot be built is skipped, leaving the
/// node to run as an ordinary single node — a degraded shape beats a refused
/// launch.
fn attach_subplans(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    plan: &mut Plan,
    seed: &[commands::course::CoursePiece],
) -> Result<()> {
    if seed.len() != plan.tasks.len() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let depth = deadreckon_core::plan::plan_depth(paths, plan);
    for (index, piece) in seed.iter().enumerate() {
        let Some(subplan) = piece.subplan.as_ref() else {
            continue;
        };
        if deadreckon_core::plan::guard_subplan_depth(depth).is_err() {
            continue;
        }
        let child_tasks = subplan
            .pieces
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(child_index, child_piece)| {
                let mut task = PlanTask::new(
                    child_index as u32,
                    commands::course::piece_subject(child_piece),
                    child_piece.goal.trim(),
                    PlanRole::Child,
                    plan.providers.default_child.clone(),
                );
                task.depends_on = child_piece
                    .depends_on
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|dependency| {
                        subplan
                            .pieces
                            .iter()
                            .position(|candidate| &candidate.id == dependency)
                            .map(|position| format!("task-{position}"))
                    })
                    .filter(|dependency| dependency != &task.task_id)
                    .collect();
                task
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let Ok(mut child) = Plan::new(
            piece.goal.trim(),
            PlanMode::FullPlan,
            child_tasks,
            plan.providers.clone(),
            plan.parent_scope.clone(),
            env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        ) else {
            continue;
        };
        child.parent_plan_id = Some(plan.plan_id.clone());
        child.owner_job_id = plan.owner_job_id.clone();
        child.parent_cwd = plan.parent_cwd.clone();
        child.acceptance_path = plan.acceptance_path.clone();
        child.capability_preview = plan.capability_preview.clone();
        child.apply = subplan.apply;
        if child.apply == deadreckon_core::plan::ApplyWhen::PerNode {
            child.on_fail = OnFail::Stop;
        }
        for task in &child.tasks {
            let spec = render_worker_spec(&child, task);
            write_worker_spec(paths, &child.plan_id, &task.task_id, &spec)?;
        }
        save_plan(paths, &child)?;
        commands::graph_job::record_plan_planner_accounting(paths, &child.plan_id, None)?;
        append_plan_event(
            paths,
            &child.plan_id,
            PlanEventKind::PlanCreated {
                mode: child.mode,
                task_count: child.tasks.len(),
            },
        )?;
        plan.tasks[index].subplan = Some(child.plan_id);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// decision came from one planner and the executed child graph from a second,
/// so a goal the classifier read as ordered could still run as N independent
/// nodes — the preview and the execution disagreeing about the same launch.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 06:35:47Z)**_

At a high level: we have built most of the system’s architecture, but we have not finished proving the full promise. The remaining work is smaller in scope but contains the most important interruption and recovery edge cases.

Nine Watchkeeper commits are on local `main`, which is nine commits ahead of `origin/main`. Together they change 118 files and add roughly 30,000 lines. A further lifecycle-hardening tranche—about 2,700 lines—is still uncommitted in the shared working tree.

## What we have implemented

| Area | Current achievement |
|---|---|
| Durable goal execution | Goals become detached local Jobs with stable IDs, isolated workspaces, append-only histories, leases, bounded retries, spend/time policies and typed terminal outcomes. |
| Recovery | The supervisor can reclaim abandoned leases, recover after process or terminal loss, and continue using the same Job identity. Actual machine-reboot survival still needs live proof. |
| Operator workflow | `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list` and `finish` understand durable Jobs and their evidence. |
| Definition of done | Approved contracts compile into deterministic checks that must pass before completion. |
| Semantic meta-judge | An independent, read-only LLM judge examines the goal, contract, changes and evidence. It cannot override failed checks. Missing or uncertain judgment does not silently become success. |
| Gate and receipts | Successful work produces an authenticated receipt bound to the contract, policy, source revision, result and evidence. Promotion and delivery validate that receipt. |
| Unified job model | Single runs, graphs/plans and campaigns now use the same durable scheduler. Chains, orchestration and direct runs are being converged through this boundary. |
| Crash-safe launch | Child launch has a durable preparation record, attempt fencing, PID/process identity and private release handshake. Crashes before release can recover without charging another logical attempt; acknowledged work can be adopted after supervisor loss. |
| Evidence protection | Synthetic, malformed, corrupt and over-budget completion evidence is rejected. Provider routes have additional protection against reading or modifying gate authority. |
| Documentation | The durable protocol, operator contract, schemas, architecture and acceptance checklist are documented. See [WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md). |
| Dogfood machinery | There is a 24-task trial matrix, adversarial scripts and metrics collection. Seven credential-free fault scenarios pass. This is test infrastructure and preliminary evidence—not yet the complete real-world trial. |

The newest uncommitted tranche also adds:

- Job ownership for Plan and Campaign artifacts.
- Frozen definitions and lineage so an agent cannot quietly rewrite scheduled work.
- Exact, single-use delegation capabilities for nested work.
- Removal of supervisor secrets from delegated child environments.
- Pre-reserved Campaign child Plan IDs, closing several duplicate-work crash windows.
- A separate feature-gated characterization executable, so legacy test behavior cannot be unlocked in the normal product binary.
- A digest-only guarded-launch record so the private launch capability is not left readable on disk.

## What the audits found still needs fixing

Four significant lifecycle gaps remain:

1. **Cancellation must always win.**  
   If cancellation arrives while an advanced child is running, its exit can currently enter recovery and relaunch work. It must finish exactly once as `Cancelled`, with no subsequent retry.

2. **Adopted advanced work needs normal recovery.**  
   A Graph or Campaign child adopted after supervisor loss is classified too early. It must follow the same bounded recovery rules as a normally launched child.

3. **Repair crashes between artifact creation and mapping.**  
   A crash after saving a root Plan/Campaign but before writing its Job mapping can strand valid work. Recovery must find that same artifact, validate its ownership, restore the mapping and preserve its real planner accounting—never create a replacement.

4. **Distinguish spend exhaustion from time exhaustion.**  
   Graph and Campaign failures need to retain a typed `SpendCap` or `WallCap` cause. Some current paths collapse these into `FatalProvider` or incorrectly report every budget failure as spend.

Work on the data structures for items 3 and 4 has begun, but it is mid-flight and not yet verified.

## What remains on the docket

In order:

1. Finish those four lifecycle fixes and add terminal-once protection.
2. Add focused cancellation, adoption, mapping-repair and spend/wall tests.
3. Add root-creation crash failpoints and verify recovery preserves the original Job and artifact IDs.
4. Run formatting, Clippy, focused tests and the complete `make verify` gate.
5. Perform the plain-language operator acceptance checklist and commit this tranche.
6. Run 20–30 real tasks across several repositories and providers.
7. During those trials, kill the terminal, worker, supervisor and machine; remove network access; tamper with gate data; and run DeadReckon on itself.
8. Measure verified completion, recovery, false acceptance/rejection, interventions, explanation quality, time and cost.
9. Simplify remaining legacy command surfaces once the job-first route has proven itself.
10. Push local `main` or open an integration PR only when you explicitly request it.

So the honest status is:

> The engine, verification model, gate and receipt system exist. The remaining work is to close several high-risk recovery races and then prove through real hostile trials that the system deserves the word “durable.”

The committed foundation was fully verified. The current uncommitted tranche passed formatting, Clippy and focused suites at an earlier checkpoint, but subsequent audit-driven edits are unfinished, so the present working tree should not yet be treated as build-green.

/// Schema 2 adds the execution-policy fields (`apply`, `on_fail`,

/// `attempts`. Every addition is `#[serde(default)]`, so schema-1 files load
/// unchanged and no migration step is required.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum PlanMode {
    FullPlan,
    Review,
}

/// Immutable accounting for the provider call that created a root Plan or
/// Campaign decomposition.
///
/// This lives in the root artifact as well as the richer accounting sidecar so
/// a crash after the artifact write cannot make recovery silently forget
/// planner spend or wall time.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RootPlannerAccounting {
    pub schema_version: u32,
    pub planner_invoked: bool,
    pub provider: Option<String>,
    pub model: Option<String>,
    pub input_tokens: u64,
    pub output_tokens: u64,
    pub cost_usd: f64,
    pub subscription: bool,
    pub wall_seconds: f64,
    pub recorded_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum BudgetDimension {
    Spend,
    Wall,
}

impl PlanMode {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::FullPlan => "full-plan",
            Self::Review => "review",
        }
    }
}

fn live_lease_refusal(error: &CliError) -> bool {
    error.to_string().contains("live lease held by owner")
}

fn supervisor_test_failpoint(name: &str) {
    if std::env::var(SUPERVISOR_FAILPOINT_ENABLE_ENV).as_deref() == Ok("1")
        && std::env::var(SUPERVISOR_FAILPOINT_ENV).as_deref() == Ok(name)
    {
        std::process::exit(86);
    }
}

fn boot_identity() -> String {
    if let Some(value) = std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_BOOT_ID")
        && !value.is_empty()
    {
        return value.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    if let Ok(value) = fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id") {
        let value = value.trim();
        if !value.is_empty() {
            return value.to_string();
        }
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    if let Ok(output) = Command::new("sysctl")
        .args(["-n", "kern.boottime"])
        .output()
        && output.status.success()
    {
        let value = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
        let value = value.trim();
        if !value.is_empty() {
            return format!("macos:{value}");
        }
    }
    // Unknown is deliberately stable. A random per-process value would look
    // like a reboot and could reclaim a live lease; stable unknown instead
    // waits for normal expiry and fails safely.
    "unknown-boot".to_string()
}

fn process_start_identity(pid: u32) -> Option<String> {
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    {
        let raw = fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/stat")).ok()?;
        let command_end = raw.rfind(')')?;
        let fields = raw[command_end + 1..]
            .split_whitespace()
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        // `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 is process start ticks. The slice starts
        // at field 3 (`state`), so index 19 is the stable same-boot identity.
            current_lease_epoch: 0,
            attempt_count: 0,
            child_run_ids: Vec::new(),
            delivery: None,
            updated_at: None,
            caveats: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_terminal(&self) -> bool {
        self.phase == JobPhase::Terminal
    }
}

impl JobView {
    pub fn load(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        let job = load_job(paths, job_id)?;
        let history = read_job_history(&paths.job_events(job_id))?;
        let projection = reduce_job_history(&job.job_id, &history)?;
        let mut attempts = Vec::new();
        let mut missing_attempts = Vec::new();
        for run_id in &projection.child_run_ids {
            match RunView::load(paths, &job.scope, run_id) {
                Ok(view) => attempts.push(view),
                Err(_) => missing_attempts.push(run_id.clone()),
            }
        }
        Ok(Self {
            job,
            projection,
            attempts,
            missing_attempts,
        })
    }
}

fn lease_expiry(now: DateTime<Utc>, ttl: Duration) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {
    if ttl.is_zero() {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "job lease ttl must be greater than zero".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    let delta = TimeDelta::from_std(ttl).map_err(|_| {
        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("job lease ttl is outside chrono range".to_string())
    })?;
    now.checked_add_signed(delta)
        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("job lease expiry overflow".to_string()))
}

fn lease_event(
    lease: &JobLease,
    sequence: JobEventSequence,
    disposition: LeaseClaimDisposition,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<JobEvent> {
    let mut detail = match serde_json::to_value(lease).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
        path: std::path::PathBuf::from("lease.json"),
        source,
    })? {
        Value::Object(detail) => detail,
        _ => Map::new(),
    };
    if let LeaseClaimDisposition::Reclaimed(reason) = disposition {
        detail.insert(
            "reclaim_reason".to_string(),
            Value::String(reason.as_str().to_string()),
        );
    }
    let event_id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
    Ok(JobEvent {
        schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
        job_id: lease.job_id.clone(),
        sequence,
        event_id,
        causation_id: format!(
            "lease-claim:{}:{}:{}",
            lease.job_id, lease.owner_id, lease.epoch
        ),
        timestamp: now,
        lease_epoch: lease.epoch,
        kind: match disposition {
            LeaseClaimDisposition::Acquired => JobEventKind::LeaseAcquired,
            LeaseClaimDisposition::Reclaimed(_) => JobEventKind::LeaseReclaimed,
        },
        detail: Value::Object(detail),
    })
}

fn lease_error(job_id: &JobId, detail: &str) -> DeadreckonError {
    DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("job lease {}: {detail}", job_id))
}

/// Append one worker lifecycle fact only when its lease epoch is still current.
pub fn append_fenced_job_event(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
    event: &JobEvent,
) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let lock_path = paths.job_dir(token.job_id.as_ref()).join(JOB_CONTROL_LOCK);
    let lock = open_job_control_lock(&lock_path)?;
    FileExt::lock_exclusive(&lock).with_path(&lock_path)?;

    let lease = load_job_lease(paths, &token.job_id)?;
    validate_token(&lease, token, now)?;
    if event.job_id != token.job_id {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!("event belongs to {}", event.job_id),
        ));
    }
    if event.lease_epoch != token.epoch {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!(
                "event lease epoch {} does not match token epoch {}",
                event.lease_epoch, token.epoch
            ),
        ));
    }
    append_job_event_locked(paths, event)
}

pub fn load_job_lease(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &JobId) -> Result<JobLease> {
    let path = paths.job_lease(job_id.as_ref());
    let raw = fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
    let lease: JobLease = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
    if lease.job_id != *job_id {
        return Err(lease_error(
            job_id,
            &format!("lease checkpoint belongs to {}", lease.job_id),
        ));
    }
    Ok(lease)
}

async fn monitor_child(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    mut child: MonitoredChild,
) -> Result<ChildExit> {
    loop {
        let status = match &mut child {
            MonitoredChild::Owned(child) => child.try_wait()?,
            MonitoredChild::Adopted(pid) if !pid_is_alive(*pid) => {
                return Ok(ChildExit {
                    status: None,
                    adopted: true,
                });
            }
            MonitoredChild::Adopted(_) => None,
        };
        if let Some(status) = status {
            return Ok(ChildExit {
                status: Some(status),
                adopted: false,
            });
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL).await;
        heartbeat_job_lease(paths, token, Utc::now(), LEASE_TTL)?;
    }
}

async fn classify_job_attempt(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    job: &Job,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: ChildExit,
    attempts_exhausted: bool,
) -> Result<()> {
    match job.shape {
        JobShape::Single => classify_persisted_attempt(paths, job, token, exit, attempts_exhausted),
        JobShape::Graph | JobShape::LegacyCampaign => {
            classify_advanced_attempt(paths, job, token, exit).await
        }
        JobShape::LegacyChain => fail_advanced_attempt(
            paths,
            token,
            exit,
            StopReason::FatalProvider,
            "legacy chain execution is not available through the durable supervisor",
        ),
    }
}

fn maybe_schedule_leaf_retry(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    job: &Job,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: &ChildExit,
    attempt: u32,
    max_attempts: u32,
) -> Result<bool> {
    if attempt >= max_attempts {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let Ok(state) = load_run(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) else {
        // Without persisted run state there is no isolated checkpoint to
        // continue safely. The caller classifies this as a terminal failure.
        return Ok(false);
    };
    let terminal_by_policy = state
        .max_spend_usd
        .is_some_and(|cap| state.total_spend_usd >= cap)
        || state
            .max_wall_seconds
            .is_some_and(|cap| state.total_wall_seconds >= cap);
    if terminal_by_policy {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let retry_stop_reason = match state.status {
        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Pending
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Planned
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Executing => StopReason::LostContainment,
        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Failed
            if state.provider_failure == Some(ProviderFailureDisposition::Retryable) =>
        {
            StopReason::TransientProvider
        }
        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Completed
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Killed
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Failed => return Ok(false),
    };

    append_attempt_stopped(
        paths,
        token,
        retry_stop_reason,
        json!({
            "attempt": attempt,
            "exit": exit_detail(exit),
            "run_status": state.status,
            "failure_reason": state.failure_reason,
            "provider_failure": state.provider_failure,
            "reason": "worker stopped with a resumable isolated run"
        }),
    )?;
    append_control_event(
        paths,
        token,
        JobEventKind::RetryScheduled,
        format!("leaf-retry:{}:{attempt}", token.epoch),
        json!({
            "after_attempt": attempt,
            "reason": "resume_persisted_run"
        }),
    )?;
    Ok(true)
}
