async fn drive_campaign(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
    driver: DriverSpec,
) -> Result<()> {
    let authority: deadreckon_protocol::JobAuthority =
        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(paths.job_authority(job.job_id.as_ref()))?)?;
    let args = commands::campaign::CampaignArgs {
        goal: job.goal.clone(),
        n: driver.child_count,
        planner_provider: driver.planner_provider,
        provider: driver.child_provider,
        planner_model: None,
        model: driver.model,
        max_spend: Some(job.policy.max_spend_usd),
        max_wall_seconds: Some(job.policy.max_wall_seconds as f64),
        sandbox: Some(authority.sandbox_requested),
        acceptance: Some(commands::job::job_acceptance_path(
            paths,
            job.job_id.as_ref(),
        )),
        preview: false,
        yes: true,
        no_hints: true,
        quiet: true,
        plain: true,
        narrate: false,
        no_narrate: true,
        narrator_model: None,
    };
    if driver_state_path(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()).is_file() {
        commands::campaign::resume_campaign_job(paths, job, &args).await
    } else {
        commands::campaign::campaign_command(args).await
    }
}

/// Verify a merged graph as the parent Job's result.
///
/// The orchestration merge run is a compatibility artifact with its own
/// random identity and a synthetic marker. It is useful evidence, but it is
/// not completion authority. This function copies that actual merged result
/// into a run whose identity is the durable Job, executes the native gate
/// there, asks a fresh read-only semantic judge, and seals with the existing
/// two-key receipt implementation.
pub(crate) async fn complete_merged_plan_parent(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
    authority: &deadreckon_protocol::JobAuthority,
    plan: &deadreckon_core::plan::Plan,
) -> Result<ParentCompletion> {
    let merged_run_id = plan.merged_run_id.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| {
        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "merged graph {} has no evidence-bearing result run",

    if let Ok(existing) = deadreckon_core::load_run(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) {

            .failure_reason

+                deadreckon_core::plan::PlanMode::FullPlan => DriverKind::FullPlan,

+                || plan.owner_job_id.as_deref() != Some(job.job_id.as_ref())
+                || plan.parent_plan_id.is_some()
+                || plan.root_goal != job.goal
+                || plan.parent_scope.as_deref() != Some(job.scope.as_str())
+                || plan.parent_cwd.as_deref() != Some(job.source_cwd.as_path())
+                || plan.acceptance_path.as_deref()
+                    != Some(commands::job::job_acceptance_path(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()).as_path())
+                || driver.kind != expected_kind

+                    plan.plan_id

fn record_parent_semantic_accounting(
    state: &mut deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
    semantic: &deadreckon_runtime::semantic_judge::SemanticJudgeRun,
) -> Result<()> {
    let accounting = &semantic.accounting;
    state.total_spend_usd += accounting.cost_usd;
    state.total_wall_seconds += accounting.wall_time_seconds;
    deadreckon_core::append_spend(
        state,
        &SpendRecord {
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            turn: state.turn,
            provider: accounting.provider.clone(),
            model: accounting.model.clone(),
            input_tokens: accounting.input_tokens,
            output_tokens: accounting.output_tokens,
            cost_usd: accounting.cost_usd,
            total_cost_usd: state.total_spend_usd,
            cap_usd: Some(job.policy.max_spend_usd),
            subscription: accounting.subscription,
            estimated: false,
            wall_time_seconds: Some(accounting.wall_time_seconds),
            wall_time_cap_seconds: Some(job.policy.max_wall_seconds as f64),
            kind: "semantic_judge".to_string(),
        },
    )?;
    let (event, reason) = match &semantic.result {
        deadreckon_runtime::SemanticJudgeResult::Achieved(_) => ("semantic_judge.achieved", None),
        deadreckon_runtime::SemanticJudgeResult::Revise(_) => ("semantic_judge.revise", None),
        deadreckon_runtime::SemanticJudgeResult::NeedsReview(_) => {
            ("semantic_judge.uncertain", None)
        }
        deadreckon_runtime::SemanticJudgeResult::Unavailable(reason) => {
            ("semantic_judge.unavailable", Some(reason.as_str()))
        }
    };
    deadreckon_core::append_trace(
        state,
        &TraceRecord {
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
            turn: state.turn,
            event: event.to_string(),
            latency_ms: Some((accounting.wall_time_seconds.max(0.0) * 1_000.0).round() as u128),
            detail: json!({
                "provider": accounting.provider,
                "model": accounting.model,
                "input_tokens": accounting.input_tokens,
                "output_tokens": accounting.output_tokens,
                "spend_usd": accounting.cost_usd,
                "wall_time_seconds": accounting.wall_time_seconds,
                "sandbox_backend": accounting.sandbox_backend,
                "workspace_access": "read-only",
                "worker_session": false,
                "decision": semantic.result.judgment().map(|judgment| judgment.decision),
                "reason": reason,
                "graph_parent": true,
            }),
        },
    )?;
    deadreckon_core::save_state(state)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn parent_needs_review(
    state: &mut deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
    reason: &str,
    decision: Option<SemanticDecision>,
    stop_reason: StopReason,
) -> Result<ParentCompletion> {
    state.failure_reason = Some(format!("NEEDS_REVIEW: {reason}"));
    state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), PhaseStatus::Failed)?;
    deadreckon_core::save_state(state)?;
    Ok(ParentCompletion::NeedsReview {
        reason: reason.to_string(),
        decision,
        stop_reason,
    })
}

fn driver_shape_error(job_id: &str) -> CliError {
    CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
        "advanced driver kind does not match job {job_id}"
    )))
}

/// Floors keep a retry from launching with a budget too small to do anything
/// but fail again — a $0.001 run is a wasted spawn, not a second chance.
const MIN_RETRY_SPEND_USD: f64 = 0.01;
const MIN_RETRY_WALL_SECONDS: f64 = 5.0;

/// What a cap has left for another attempt. Uncapped and exhausted are
/// different answers and must not share a representation: one launches a
/// retry with no limit, the other refuses it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum RetryBudget {
    Uncapped,
    Remaining(f64),
    Exhausted,
}

fn remaining_retry_budget(cap: Option<f64>, spent: f64, floor: f64) -> RetryBudget {
    let Some(cap) = cap else {
        return RetryBudget::Uncapped;
    };
    let remaining = (cap - spent).max(0.0);
    if remaining >= floor {
        RetryBudget::Remaining(remaining)
    } else {
        RetryBudget::Exhausted
    }
}

+fn plan_budget_exhaustion(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    plan_id: &str,
+) -> Result<Option<(StopReason, String)>> {
+    let event = deadreckon_core::read_plan_events(paths, plan_id)?
+        .into_iter()
+        .rev()
+        .find_map(|event| match event.event {
+            deadreckon_core::PlanEventKind::TaskBudgetExhausted {
+                dimension, reason, ..
+            } => Some((dimension, reason)),
+            _ => None,
+        });
+    Ok(event.map(|(dimension, reason)| {
+        let stop_reason = match dimension {
+            deadreckon_core::plan::BudgetDimension::Spend => StopReason::SpendCap,
+            deadreckon_core::plan::BudgetDimension::Wall => StopReason::WallCap,
+        };
+        (stop_reason, reason)
+    }))
+}
+
+fn campaign_budget_exhaustion(
+    campaign_dir: &Path,
+) -> Result<Option<(StopReason, String)>> {
+    let event = deadreckon_core::campaign::read_campaign_events(campaign_dir)?
+        .into_iter()
+        .rev()
+        .find(|event| event.kind == "budget_exhausted");
+    let Some(event) = event else {
+        return Ok(None);
+    };
+    let stop_reason = match event.detail.get("stop_reason") {
+        Some(value) => serde_json::from_value::<StopReason>(value.clone())?,
+        None => StopReason::SpendCap,
+    };
+    if !matches!(stop_reason, StopReason::SpendCap | StopReason::WallCap) {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "campaign budget event names non-budget stop reason {stop_reason:?}"
+        ))));
+    }
+    let reason = event
+        .detail
+        .get("reason")
+        .and_then(Value::as_str)
+        .map(ToString::to_string)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| match stop_reason {
+            StopReason::SpendCap => "campaign tree spend budget was exhausted".to_string(),
+            StopReason::WallCap => "campaign tree wall-time budget was exhausted".to_string(),
+            _ => unreachable!(),
+        });
+    Ok(Some((stop_reason, reason)))
+}
+
+fn finish_advanced_budget_attempt(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    exit: ChildExit,
+    stop_reason: StopReason,
+    artifact: &str,
+    reason: &str,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    append_attempt_stopped(
+        paths,
+        token,
+        stop_reason,
+        json!({
+            "exit": exit_detail(&exit),
+            "artifact": artifact,
+            "reason": reason,
+        }),
+    )?;
+    append_terminal_event(
+        paths,
+        token,
+        JobEventKind::BudgetExhausted,
+        stop_reason,
+        json!({
+            "reason": reason,
+            "artifact": artifact,
+        }),
+    )?;
+    Ok(())
+}

    fn plan_on_disk(paths: &DeadreckonPaths) -> Plan {

            plain: true,

            RetryBudget::Exhausted,
            "overspend must not wrap into a fresh allowance"

/// Read a sub-orchestrator's published plan id, if it has reached plan creation.
pub(crate) fn read_sub_plan_id(launch_dir: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    fs::read_to_string(launch_dir.join(SUB_PLAN_ID_FILE))
        .ok()
        .map(|raw| raw.trim().to_string())
        .filter(|plan_id| !plan_id.is_empty())
}

pub(crate) fn campaign_test_failpoint(name: &str) {
    if std::env::var("DEADRECKON_TEST_CAMPAIGN_FAILPOINTS").as_deref() == Ok("1")
        && std::env::var("DEADRECKON_TEST_CAMPAIGN_FAILPOINT").as_deref() == Ok(name)
    {
        std::process::exit(86);
    }
}

/// Write a sub-orchestrator's result sidecar. Called at the end of
/// `orchestrate full-plan` when launched by a campaign (DEADRECKON_CAMPAIGN_SUB_RESULT
/// is set): records the plan id and its merged result run for the meta-coordinator.
pub(crate) fn record_sub_orchestrator_result(
    plan_id: &str,
    launch_dir: &Path,
    ok: bool,
        println!(
            "{}",
            ui_status(format!(
                "{task_id} subplan {} merged into run {}",
                run_prefix(subplan_id),
                run_prefix(&merged_run_id)
            ))
        );
    }
    Ok(merged_run_id)
}

#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
fn plan_test_failpoint(name: &str) {
    if std::env::var("DEADRECKON_TEST_PLAN_FAILPOINT").as_deref() == Ok(name) {
        panic!("deadreckon plan test failpoint: {name}");
    }
}

#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))]
fn plan_test_failpoint(_name: &str) {}

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 07:02:23Z)**_

The public crash test caught a real timing mistake: mapping repair ran only when a new supervisor claimed the Job. In this failure, the existing supervisor observes the driver crash immediately and classifies it before restarting. I’m moving repair into the shared post-child reconciliation point so both same-process recovery and supervisor-restart recovery use it.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 07:08:37Z)**_

The short version: DeadReckon’s core promise is now substantially implemented. We are no longer designing the durable executor; we are hardening it and proving that it survives awkward failure boundaries.

It is feature-complete enough to begin serious dogfooding, but not yet confidence-complete.

## What has been implemented

### 1. One durable Job model

`start` now creates a durable, detached Job with:

- a stable Job ID;
- append-only lifecycle history;
- leases and heartbeats;
- bounded retries;
- recovery after supervisor or worker interruption;
- explicit outcomes such as cancelled, blocked, budget exhausted, failed and needs review;
- `attach`, `status`, `list`, `report` and `finish` operations.

Direct runs, graphs/plans and campaigns now enter through this common supervisor instead of behaving as unrelated execution systems.

### 2. Two-key completion

A result cannot be accepted merely because an agent says it is done.

Completion requires:

1. Deterministic checks from the definition of done.
2. A separate, read-only semantic judge evaluating the goal, changes and evidence.

The semantic judge cannot overrule failed checks. Missing, malformed, synthetic or insufficient evidence fails closed instead of producing an accepted result.

### 3. Protected completion receipts

DeadReckon now creates authenticated receipts that bind the result to:

- the contract and policy;
- source and resulting revisions;
- deterministic evidence;
- semantic judgment;
- spend and timing information;
- delivery/promotion information.

Gate authority and signing material are kept outside the worker’s visible workspace. We added adversarial cases for forged acknowledgements, fabricated evidence and altered histories.

### 4. Crash-safe launching and recovery

Launching a coding CLI is now treated as a durable protocol:

- the launch is recorded before the worker is released;
- a private capability handshake controls release;
- PID, boot and process-start identity are recorded;
- an existing worker can be adopted after supervisor loss;
- stale or reused PIDs are rejected;
- crashes before release do not consume a logical attempt;
- cancellation wins over retry or later classification;
- terminal outcomes should be written only once.

Graph and Campaign recovery continue under the original Job and root artifact IDs rather than silently creating replacement work.

### 5. Durable nested work

The current hardening tranche adds:

- Campaign child Plan IDs reserved before launch;
- one-time delegation capabilities;
- frozen Plan/Campaign definitions and lineage;
- recovery from crashes between artifact creation and mapping publication;
- reconstruction of missing mappings without replanning;
- exact preservation of root planner usage;
- shared recovery rules for owned and adopted workers.

### 6. Bounded spend and time

Planner and worker accounting is being embedded in the durable artifacts rather than reconstructed from optional sidecars.

Spend-cap and wall-time exhaustion are now recorded as different typed reasons and propagated into the final Job outcome.

### 7. Documentation and dogfood infrastructure

We added:

- the durable operator contract;
- architecture and lifecycle documentation;
- an operator acceptance guide;
- a 24-task dogfood harness;
- seven passing credential-free adversarial scenarios;
- CI/release coverage for the special characterization executable.

## Where the code is

There are currently two layers of work:

- Nine completed commits are on your local `main`.
- A further hardening tranche—about 4,000 inserted lines across 26 relevant files—is still uncommitted while verification is underway.

Important correction: the nine commits are ahead of `origin/main`, but they have not been pushed. The work is already integrated into the local `main`; it is not sitting in separate agent branches. The three subagents completed focused audits, while implementation occurred in the shared worktree.

I will not push anything without your direction.

## What is still on the docket

### Immediate landing work

One supervisor test currently fails:

- when machine boot identity changes, the recovered Job becomes `Blocked`;
- the test expected `RetryExhausted`.

That needs diagnosis before deciding whether the implementation or expected result is wrong.

There is also one remaining crash/budget boundary to close: if root planning exhausts its budget and the process dies between saving the Plan/Campaign and publishing its mapping, recovery must classify it as spend- or wall-budget exhausted before any child work can start.

After that:

- run focused recovery and fault tests;
- run the full repository verification gate;
- perform the operator acceptance checklist;
- review and commit the hardening tranche.

### Proof still required

The largest remaining work is evidence, not another major architectural layer:

- run 20–30 real tasks across repositories and providers;
- kill the supervisor, worker, terminal and actual machine;
- test real reboot/service restart recovery;
- test network removal and restoration;
- run tampering attempts from the worker’s perspective;
- run Linux and Windows recovery tests;
- measure false acceptance, false rejection, intervention rate, recovery rate and judging cost;
- run DeadReckon on DeadReckon repeatedly.

### Product simplification still required

The common Job model exists, but old terminology and compatibility paths remain visible. We still need to decide how aggressively to move Plans, Chains and Campaigns behind an advanced namespace and make the ordinary experience feel like simply:

```text
start
attach
status
list
finish
```

Some duplicate Plan/Campaign histories and compatibility machinery also remain. They are now subordinate to Job lifecycle truth, but they still add maintenance cost.

## Why it has taken so long

The scope crossed every execution path in an established codebase. Crash safety is also unusually expensive: it is not enough to make the happy path work. Every write, process launch and state transition has to answer, “What happens if the machine dies immediately after this line?”

The necessary complexity is:

- durable history;
- leasing and fencing;
- stable identities;
- bounded recovery;
- two independent completion keys;
- budget enforcement;
- protected receipts.

The incidental complexity is mainly:

- migrating several older execution models without breaking them;
- parallel Plan, Chain and Campaign representations;
- compatibility and characterization-only pathways;
- filesystem durability differences across operating systems;
- repeatedly discovering obscure crash windows through adversarial tests.

So what is happening now is a hardening loop, not uncontrolled feature expansion. Tests expose a boundary, we make that boundary durable, and then test the adjacent boundaries. The remaining question is no longer “Can DeadReckon do this?” It is “Have we produced enough hostile evidence to trust that it consistently does this?”

The failure is a real regression, not a stale assertion: the new advanced-artifact repair helper validates a Graph/Campaign driver specification before checking the Job shape, so an ordinary Single Job is incorrectly declared corrupt before reboot recovery runs. +    accounting: &deadreckon_core::plan::RootPlannerAccounting,
+    max_spend_usd: f64,
+    max_wall_seconds: f64,
+) -> Result<Option<RootPlannerBudgetExhaustion>> {
+    validate_root_planner_accounting(accounting)?;
+    if accounting.cost_usd >= max_spend_usd {
+        return Ok(Some(RootPlannerBudgetExhaustion {
+            dimension: deadreckon_core::plan::BudgetDimension::Spend,
+            stop_reason: StopReason::SpendCap,
+            reason: format!(
+                "root planner exhausted the approved spend cap before child launch (${:.6} used of ${max_spend_usd:.6})",
+                accounting.cost_usd
+            ),
+        }));
+    }
+    if accounting.wall_seconds >= max_wall_seconds {
+        return Ok(Some(RootPlannerBudgetExhaustion {
+            dimension: deadreckon_core::plan::BudgetDimension::Wall,
+            stop_reason: StopReason::WallCap,
+            reason: format!(
+                "root planner exhausted the approved wall-time cap before child launch ({:.3}s used of {max_wall_seconds:.3}s)",
+                accounting.wall_seconds
+            ),
+        }));
+    }
+    Ok(None)
+}

+    let wall = max_wall_seconds.map(|cap| {

+        )

+    Ok(Ok(PlanTaskBudgetShares {

+    }))
+}

+                dimension: exhaustion.dimension,
+                reason: exhaustion.reason.clone(),
+            },
+        )?;
+    }
+    plan.status = PlanStatus::Failed;
+    plan.conductor_pid = None;

+        let decision =
+            plan_task_budget_shares(&budget_plan(), Some(5.0), Some(40.0), true)
+                .expect("budget shares");
+        let PlanTaskBudgetDecision::Shares(shares) = decision else {
+            panic!("planner should leave child budget");
+        };
+        let spend = shares.spend.into_iter().flatten().collect::<Vec<_>>();
+        let wall = shares.wall.into_iter().flatten().collect::<Vec<_>>();
+        assert!((spend.iter().sum::<f64>() - 3.0).abs() < 0.000_001);
+        assert!((wall.iter().sum::<f64>() - 30.0).abs() < 0.000_001);
+        assert!(spend.iter().all(|share| *share <= 1.0));
+        assert!(wall.iter().all(|share| *share <= 10.0));
+    }

+                .expect("legacy budget")
+        else {

+        };

# Map of DeadReckon

Status: repository analysis updated 2026-07-29 through the Watchkeeper
convergence and credential-free adversarial trials.

## Executive map

DeadReckon is not primarily another coding agent. It is an outer control plane for coding agents and agent harnesses. The inner harness proposes and performs work; DeadReckon owns the durable run, isolation, budgets, evidence, independent completion decision, recovery, and promotion.

Its irreducible pattern is:

```text
goal + definition of done
          |
          v
isolated, durable Job -----> provider / inner harness does work
          |                              |
          +<---- events, spend, diffs, snapshots, provenance
          |
          v
contained checks + independent semantic judge
          |
          +---- fail/revise: retain evidence, continue or stop explicitly
          |
          +---- pass: seal receipt, then promote deliberately
```

That is the essential product. The strongest reason for it to exist is the gap between *an agent saying it is done* and *an operator being able to trust, inspect, recover, and accept the result*. This matches the original unmet-needs research: predictable delegation needed operational infrastructure more than another transcript or chat surface.

The repository now contains three different things which should not be judged alike:

1. A differentiated Job kernel: immutable authority, append-only lifecycle,
   fenced local supervision and isolated work across guided and ordinary
   direct execution. Durable Single, Graph and Campaign Jobs prove 2
   independent completion decisions before deliberate promotion. Preserve and
   dogfood this.
2. Established graph/campaign conductors, direct advanced commands, reports,
   imports, and narration. Ordinary direct orchestration, new chains,
   stored-plan forks and campaigns now run those conductors under a parent Job
   and verify the merged parent. Explicit compatibility modes and chain
   extension remain process-owned.
3. Compatibility layers, speculative depth, and incomplete bets. Deprecate or
   quarantine these rather than allowing them to obscure the kernel.

## How maturity is assessed

Maturity here means engineering evidence in this repository, not market adoption.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Hardened** | Central path, persistent model, broad tests, recovery/error semantics and established user surface. |
| **Stable / bounded** | Real and tested, but deliberately narrower than the whole unmet need. |
| **Maturing** | Substantive implementation with a known parity, safety, migration or operability gap. |
| **Experimental** | Working implementation whose product demand or abstraction boundary is not yet established. |
| **Compatibility-only** | Retained for old scripts or naming; not a product direction. |
| **Absent** | The underlying need is not currently addressed, even if nearby primitives exist. |

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 07:34:21Z)**_

The core Watchkeeper promise is now substantially implemented. What remains is less “invent the system” and more “finish hardening it, prove it under real failures, and remove the older competing paths.”

I would describe DeadReckon today as functionally assembled, but not yet operationally proven.

## Progress against the original five outcomes

| Outcome | Current state |
|---|---|
| Durable goal executor | Largely implemented |
| Deterministic checks plus semantic meta-judge | Implemented for durable Jobs |
| Protected gate and tamper-resistant receipt | Implemented and adversarially tested |
| One Job model for runs, plans, chains and campaigns | Mostly implemented; compatibility paths remain |
| 20–30-task real-world dogfooding | Mostly not done |

## Features implemented

### Durable Job execution

DeadReckon now has a real durable Job layer above individual coding runs:

- immutable approved goal, definition of done and policy;
- append-only Job lifecycle;
- fenced leases so two supervisors cannot legitimately own one Job;
- detached supervision;
- process-group ownership and cancellation;
- recovery of abandoned attempts;
- bounded retries, spend and wall time;
- typed terminal outcomes such as completed, blocked, cancelled, failed and budget exhausted;
- persisted `JobView` state that `status`, `list`, `attach` and `finish` can read after the launching terminal disappears.

A user service can restart the supervisor after login. The machinery exists, but actual reboot recovery has not yet passed a live operator trial.

### Two independent completion decisions

A durable Job cannot complete merely because the coding agent says it is done.

The path now requires:

1. The deterministic definition-of-done gate passes inside the contained workspace.
2. A fresh, read-only semantic judge assesses the approved goal, contract, result, diff and evidence.
3. The supervisor validates both decisions before issuing the receipt and permitting promotion.

A failed deterministic gate cannot be overridden by the semantic judge. Semantic `revise` or uncertainty stops the Job without calling it verified.

### Protected gate and receipt boundary

The trust boundary was materially strengthened:

- native markers and final receipts use HMAC-SHA-256;
- signing material lives outside the delegated workspace;
- authority, gate, proof and receipt paths are protected from the coding agent;
- receipts bind the approved contract and policy to the source revision, resulting revision, evidence and confinement posture;
- uncontained or `sandbox none` execution cannot earn a strict verified receipt;
- `finish` revalidates the receipt before exporting or promoting the result;
- synthetic completion evidence and tampered receipts are rejected.

### Execution converging on one Job model

The following ordinary launches now create durable Jobs:

- direct `run` → Single Job;
- direct `orchestrate` → Graph Job;
- stored-plan `fork` → Graph Job;
- supported new chains → linear Graph Job;
- direct `campaign` → Campaign Job;
- guided `start` modes → the appropriate Job shape.

Graph and Campaign work produce a same-ID parent result. Child results are evidence; they do not independently declare the overall goal complete.

Some intentionally explicit compatibility paths remain outside this model: historical `chain run|resume`, chain extension, previews, and explicitly in-place or uncontained execution.

### Advanced Graph and Campaign recovery

The current uncommitted tranche adds substantial hardening:

- Plan and Campaign definitions are frozen and tied to the owning Job.
- Delegated child capabilities are scoped and single-use.
- Campaign sub-plan IDs are reserved before launch and recovered under the same identity.
- Missing `driver.json` mappings can be reconstructed without creating another root.
- Child launch is crash-atomic where durable linkage exists.
- Cancellation and terminal events are written only once.
- Boot-identity changes cannot accidentally adopt an unrelated reused PID.
- Chain shapes that cannot be translated honestly are refused instead of silently losing semantics.

### Aggregate budget enforcement

The latest work closes a serious hole found during the loop:

- root planner spend and wall time are preserved durably;
- planner use is subtracted before children receive budgets;
- remaining Plan budget is divided across tasks instead of giving every task the entire parent cap;
- Campaign children now receive wall limits as well as spend limits;
- recovery checks planner exhaustion before allowing child work to resume;
- Graph and Campaign planner exhaustion becomes a typed `SpendCap` or `WallCap`;
- crash-recovery tests assert that zero children launch once the root planner has consumed the approved budget.

Focused tests for these paths are passing. The full repository gate has not yet been rerun after the newest changes.

### Operator evidence

The implementation now leaves behind:

- Job events and projections;
- linked run evidence;
- spend and timing information;
- deterministic gate results;
- semantic judgment;
- source/result lineage;
- signed completion receipt;
- narratives and inspection/report surfaces.

The intended operator model is captured in the [architecture map](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md:78) and the concrete [operator acceptance script](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md:1).

## Where the code currently lives

Nine Watchkeeper commits are already committed on local `main`, which is nine commits ahead of `origin/main`. They have not been pushed.

A further hardening tranche is still uncommitted: roughly 4,866 additions and 507 removals across 26 relevant code, test and build files. Unrelated `.specstory`, editor and personal working-tree changes are being kept out of that tranche.

So there are currently two integration layers:

- committed locally on `main`;
- implemented in the working tree but awaiting complete verification and a local commit.

Nothing reaches remote `main` until the remaining tranche passes verification, is committed deliberately, and you authorize a push.

## Still on the docket

### Immediate engineering completion

- Format the current tranche.
- Rerun the complete supervisor, Plan, Campaign, chain and ownership suites.
- Run Clippy with warnings denied.
- Run the full `make verify` gate.
- Inspect the final patch and ensure no user-owned files are included.
- Execute the operator acceptance checklist.
- Commit the hardening tranche locally.

### Real operational proof

This is now the largest missing piece:

- run the 20–30-task matrix across multiple repositories and providers;
- kill the worker and supervisor during real work;
- close the launching terminal;
- restart the service;
- perform an actual machine restart;
- remove network access at awkward points;
- tamper with authority, marker and receipt artifacts;
- run DeadReckon on DeadReckon;
- measure verified completion, recovery, intervention count, judge cost, comprehension time, false acceptance and false rejection.

The repository’s own map records seven credential-free adversarial passes, but the live 24-row kit has only two attempted rows, 22 not run, and zero verified completions. That is the clearest reason not to call the outcome finished yet.

### Semantic repair for Graph and Campaign Jobs

A Single Job has a bounded repair path after semantic `revise`. Graph and Campaign parents currently stop at `NEEDS_REVIEW`. They still need a safe repair design that:

- preserves frozen authority;
- does not reopen arbitrary child execution;
- produces a new auditable attempt;
- reruns both completion keys;
- cannot reuse an invalid old receipt.

### Compatibility cleanup

After dogfooding tells us which paths matter:

- preserve or retire historical chain execution;
- decide the future of chain extension;
- keep preview and uncontained execution explicitly untrusted;
- group advanced scheduling commands behind progressive disclosure;
- remove duplicate lifecycle and narration paths where they add no value.

### Platform and provider parity

Still unproven or incomplete:

- live launchd/systemd operation;
- a designed Windows service posture;
- consistent protected-path behavior across every provider adapter;
- structured event, context and steering parity between providers.

## Bottom line

Against the target statement:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify both the checks and the meaning of the result, and leave behind a clear receipt explaining what happened.

We have implemented almost every noun and mechanism in that sentence. The unresolved phrase is “will survive interruptions” as an operator-trusted claim. Automated recovery and fault-injection coverage are substantial, but live terminal, service, reboot and cross-provider trials have not earned that confidence yet.

The next phase should therefore be verification, dogfooding and pruning—not another broad feature expansion.

---
name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
---

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

Before editing, you should be able to answer, in writing: "The behavior is produced by `<file>:<lines>` because `<causal chain>`, and I will confirm the fix by `<observation/command>`." If you cannot, you have not finished diagnosing.

## Failure modes

- Patching the layer where the symptom appears (e.g. button-state code) when the real cause is elsewhere (a default selection upstream). The user rejects this with: "You got it wrong… the issue was not with the button states." Localize first.
- Jumping to a fix on the first plausible theory. Demand or construct the observation that would discriminate between candidate causes before committing to one.
- Editing during a "don't write any code yet" instruction. That instruction is a gate, not a delay — produce the mechanism trace and stop.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-04), consistently followed by the user, high adjacent-approval rate. Consolidates the read-before-write gate, fault-localization-before-fix, and mechanism-trace-before-trust patterns.

fn advanced_artifact_recoverable(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job) -> bool {
    let Ok(driver) = super::graph_job::load_driver_state(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) else {
        return false;
    };
    if driver.job_id != job.job_id || driver.artifact_id != job.job_id.as_ref() {
        return false;
    }
    match job.shape {
        JobShape::Graph if driver.artifact_kind == "plan" => {
            let Ok(plan) = deadreckon_core::plan::load_plan(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) else {
                return false;
            };
            matches!(
                plan.status,
                deadreckon_core::plan::PlanStatus::Pending
                    | deadreckon_core::plan::PlanStatus::Forked
            )
        }
        JobShape::LegacyCampaign if driver.artifact_kind == "campaign" => {
            let campaign_dir = paths.plan_dir(job.job_id.as_ref());
            let Ok(campaign) = deadreckon_core::campaign::read_campaign(&campaign_dir) else {
                return false;
            };
            matches!(
                campaign.status,
                deadreckon_core::campaign::CampaignStatus::Pending
                    | deadreckon_core::campaign::CampaignStatus::Forked
            )
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn merged_graph_waits_for_parent_completion(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job) -> bool {
    if job.shape != JobShape::Graph {
        return false;
    }
    let Ok(driver) = super::graph_job::load_driver_state(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) else {
        return false;
    };
    if driver.job_id != job.job_id
        || driver.artifact_kind != "plan"
        || driver.artifact_id != job.job_id.as_ref()
    {
        return false;
    }
    let Ok(plan) = deadreckon_core::plan::load_plan(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) else {
        return false;
    };
    plan.status == deadreckon_core::plan::PlanStatus::Merged
}

fn merged_campaign_waits_for_parent_completion(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job) -> bool {
    if job.shape != JobShape::LegacyCampaign {
        return false;
    }
    let Ok(driver) = super::graph_job::load_driver_state(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) else {
        return false;
    };
    if driver.job_id != job.job_id
        || driver.artifact_kind != "campaign"
        || driver.artifact_id != job.job_id.as_ref()
    {
        return false;
    }
    let campaign_dir = paths.plan_dir(job.job_id.as_ref());
    let Ok(campaign) = deadreckon_core::campaign::read_campaign(&campaign_dir) else {
        return false;
    };
    campaign.status == deadreckon_core::campaign::CampaignStatus::Merged
}

The fault is localized to the test fixture, not the recovery decision. `reconcile_child_exit` now validates the persisted advanced root through `recover_pending_driver_state`; that validator correctly requires a Graph Plan to name its owning Job, parent working directory and frozen acceptance contract before allowing a retry. `graph_fixture` creates a `Forked` Plan without those ownership fields, so recovery classifies the fixture as corrupt and returns `Finished`. I’ll make the shared fixture represent a valid Job-owned Plan, then confirm with the single regression and the full supervisor suite.

fn append_terminal_event(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    kind: JobEventKind,
    reason: StopReason,
    extra: Value,
) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let view = JobView::load(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())?;
    if view.projection.is_terminal() {
        return Ok(view.projection);
    }
    let cancelled = view.projection.stop_reason == Some(StopReason::CancelRequested);
    let suppressed_kind = serde_json::to_value(kind)?;
    let effective_kind = if cancelled {
        JobEventKind::Cancelled
    } else {
        kind
    };
    let effective_reason = if cancelled {
        StopReason::CancelRequested
    } else {
        reason
    };
    let effective_extra = if cancelled {
        json!({
            "reason": "operator cancellation won before terminal classification",
            "suppressed_terminal_kind": suppressed_kind,
        })
    } else {
        extra
    };
    let projection = append_control_event(
        paths,
        token,
        effective_kind,
        format!("terminal:{}:{}", token.epoch, Uuid::new_v4()),
        merge_stop_reason(effective_reason, effective_extra),
    )?;
    if !projection.is_terminal() && projection.stop_reason == Some(StopReason::CancelRequested) {
        return append_control_event(
            paths,
            token,
            JobEventKind::Cancelled,
            format!("terminal-cancelled:{}:{}", token.epoch, Uuid::new_v4()),
            merge_stop_reason(
                StopReason::CancelRequested,
                json!({
                    "reason": "operator cancellation raced terminal classification and won",
                    "suppressed_terminal_kind": suppressed_kind,
                }),
            ),
        );
    }
    Ok(projection)
}

fn finish_cancel_requested(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: Option<&ChildExit>,
) -> Result<bool> {
    let view = JobView::load(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())?;
    if view.projection.is_terminal() {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    if view.projection.stop_reason != Some(StopReason::CancelRequested) {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let history = read_job_history(&paths.job_events(token.job_id.as_ref()))?;
    let attempt_active = history
        .events()
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find_map(|event| match event.kind {
            JobEventKind::AttemptStopped => Some(false),
            JobEventKind::AttemptStarted => Some(true),
            _ => None,
        })
        .unwrap_or(false);
    if attempt_active {
        append_attempt_stopped(
            paths,
            JobOutcome::Blocked,
            detail_stop_reason(&event.detail).unwrap_or(StopReason::OperatorInputRequired),
        ),
        JobEventKind::BudgetExhausted => terminal(
            projection,
            JobOutcome::BudgetExhausted,
            detail_stop_reason(&event.detail).unwrap_or(StopReason::SpendCap),
        ),
        DeadlineReached => terminal(
            projection,
            JobOutcome::DeadlineReached,
            StopReason::Deadline,
        ),
        CancelRequested => {
            projection.phase = JobPhase::Waiting;
            projection.stop_reason = Some(StopReason::CancelRequested);
        }
        Cancelled => terminal(
            projection,
            JobOutcome::Cancelled,
            StopReason::CancelRequested,
        ),
        Failed => {
            let reason = detail_stop_reason(&event.detail).unwrap_or(StopReason::FatalProvider);
            let outcome = if reason == StopReason::AttemptLimit {
                JobOutcome::RetryExhausted
            } else {
                JobOutcome::Failed
            };
            terminal(projection, outcome, reason);
        }
        Verified => terminal(projection, JobOutcome::Verified, StopReason::Verified),
        JobEventKind::ResultApplied => {
            projection.delivery = Some(job_delivery(event, JobDeliveryKind::Applied)?);
        }
        JobEventKind::ResultExported => {
            projection.delivery = Some(job_delivery(event, JobDeliveryKind::Exported)?);
        }
        JobEventKind::ContractApproved => {}
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn terminal(projection: &mut JobProjection, outcome: JobOutcome, reason: StopReason) {
    projection.phase = JobPhase::Terminal;
    projection.outcome = Some(outcome);
    projection.stop_reason = Some(reason);
}

fn detail_string<'a>(detail: &'a Value, name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    detail.get(name).and_then(Value::as_str)
}

fn finish_cancel_requested(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: Option<&ChildExit>,
) -> Result<bool> {
    let view = JobView::load(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())?;
    if view.projection.is_terminal() {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    if view.projection.stop_reason != Some(StopReason::CancelRequested) {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let history = read_job_history(&paths.job_events(token.job_id.as_ref()))?;
    let attempt_active = history
        .events()
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find_map(|event| match event.kind {
            JobEventKind::AttemptStopped => Some(false),
            JobEventKind::AttemptStarted => Some(true),
            _ => None,
        })
        .unwrap_or(false);
    if attempt_active {
        append_attempt_stopped(
            paths,
            token,
            StopReason::CancelRequested,
            json!({
                "reason": "operator cancelled the active durable attempt",
                "exit": exit.map(exit_detail),
            }),
        )?;
    }
    append_terminal_event(
        paths,
        token,
        JobEventKind::Cancelled,
        StopReason::CancelRequested,
        json!({
            "reason": if attempt_active {
                "operator cancelled the active durable attempt"
            } else {
                "operator cancelled before another attempt was launched"
            },
        }),
    )?;
    Ok(true)
}

fn merge_stop_reason(reason: StopReason, extra: Value) -> Value {
    let mut detail = match extra {
        Value::Object(detail) => detail,
        Value::Null => serde_json::Map::new(),
        value => {
            let mut detail = serde_json::Map::new();
            detail.insert("detail".to_string(), value);
            detail
        }
    };
    detail.insert(
        "stop_reason".to_string(),
        serde_json::to_value(reason).unwrap_or(Value::String("corrupt_history".to_string())),
    );
    Value::Object(detail)
}

fn append_control_event(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    kind: JobEventKind,
    causation_id: String,
    detail: Value,
) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let now = Utc::now();
    let projection = JobView::load(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())?.projection;
    let sequence = projection
        .last_sequence
        .checked_add(1)
        .and_then(JobEventSequence::new)
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
                "job {} event sequence exhausted",
                token.job_id
            )))
        })?;
    let event = JobEvent {
        schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
        job_id: token.job_id.clone(),
        sequence,
        event_id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
        causation_id,
        timestamp: now,
        lease_epoch: token.epoch,
        kind,
        detail,
    };
    Ok(append_fenced_job_event(paths, token, now, &event)?)
}

/// Parsed lifecycle rows plus a bounded account of recoverable read damage.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct JobHistory {
    events: Vec<JobEvent>,
    raw_lines: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    pub caveats: Vec<String>,
}

impl JobHistory {
    pub fn events(&self) -> &[JobEvent] {
        &self.events
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.events.is_empty()
    }
}

/// Write immutable job identity once. A changed replacement is never allowed.
pub fn write_job(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job) -> Result<()> {
    let path = paths.job_json(job.job_id.as_ref());
    if path.exists() {
        let existing = load_job(paths, job.job_id.as_ref())?;
        return if existing == *job {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(history_corrupt(
                job.job_id.as_ref(),
                "job.json is immutable and already contains different bytes",
            ))
        };
    }
    atomic_write_json(&path, job)
}

pub fn load_job(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> Result<Job> {
    let path = paths.job_json(job_id);
    let raw = fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
    let job: Job = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
    if job.job_id.as_ref() != job_id {
        return Err(history_corrupt(
            job_id,
            &format!("job.json contains identity {}", job.job_id),
        ));
    }
    Ok(job)
}

/// Append one worker lifecycle fact only when its lease epoch is still current.
pub fn append_fenced_job_event(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
    event: &JobEvent,
) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let lock_path = paths.job_dir(token.job_id.as_ref()).join(JOB_CONTROL_LOCK);
    let lock = open_job_control_lock(&lock_path)?;
    FileExt::lock_exclusive(&lock).with_path(&lock_path)?;

    let lease = load_job_lease(paths, &token.job_id)?;
    validate_token(&lease, token, now)?;
    if event.job_id != token.job_id {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!("event belongs to {}", event.job_id),
        ));
    }
    if event.lease_epoch != token.epoch {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!(
                "event lease epoch {} does not match token epoch {}",
                event.lease_epoch, token.epoch
            ),
        ));
    }
    let history = read_job_history(&paths.job_events(event.job_id.as_ref()))?;
    let projection = reduce_job_history(&event.job_id, &history)?;
    if projection.is_terminal() {
        return Ok(projection);
    }
    if projection.stop_reason == Some(deadreckon_protocol::StopReason::CancelRequested) {
        let cancellation_stop = event.kind == JobEventKind::AttemptStopped
            && event.detail.get("stop_reason").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("cancel_requested");
        if event.kind != JobEventKind::Cancelled && !cancellation_stop {
            return Ok(projection);
        }
    }
    append_job_event_locked(paths, event)
}

pub fn load_job_lease(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &JobId) -> Result<JobLease> {
    let path = paths.job_lease(job_id.as_ref());
    let raw = fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
    let lease: JobLease = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
    if lease.job_id != *job_id {
        return Err(lease_error(
            job_id,
            &format!("lease checkpoint belongs to {}", lease.job_id),
        ));
    }
    Ok(lease)
}

fn load_job_lease_optional(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &JobId) -> Result<Option<JobLease>> {
    let path = paths.job_lease(job_id.as_ref());
    match fs::read(&path) {
        Ok(raw) => {
            let lease: JobLease = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
            if lease.job_id != *job_id {
                return Err(lease_error(
                    job_id,
                    &format!("lease checkpoint belongs to {}", lease.job_id),
                ));
            }
            Ok(Some(lease))
        }
        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
        Err(source) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io { path, source }),
    }
}

/// Append one control fact while holding the per-job lock, then checkpoint the
/// projection. The event is durable before the projection it authorizes.
pub fn append_job_event(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, event: &JobEvent) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    fs::create_dir_all(paths.job_dir(event.job_id.as_ref()))
        .with_path(paths.job_dir(event.job_id.as_ref()))?;
    let lock_path = paths.job_dir(event.job_id.as_ref()).join(JOB_CONTROL_LOCK);
    let lock = open_job_control_lock(&lock_path)?;
    lock.lock_exclusive().with_path(&lock_path)?;
    append_job_event_locked(paths, event)
}

fn validate_owner(owner: &LeaseOwner) -> Result<()> {
    if owner.owner_id.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "job lease owner_id must not be empty".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    if owner.boot_id.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "job lease boot_id must not be empty".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    if owner.pid == 0 || owner.process_group == 0 {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "job lease pid and process_group must be non-zero".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn validate_token(lease: &JobLease, token: &LeaseToken, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<()> {
    if lease.job_id != token.job_id
        || lease.owner_id != token.owner_id
        || lease.epoch != token.epoch
        || lease.boot_id != token.boot_id
    {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!(
                "stale lease token for owner {} epoch {}",
                token.owner_id, token.epoch
            ),
        ));
    }
    if lease.expires_at <= now {
        return Err(lease_error(
            &token.job_id,
            &format!(
                "lease epoch {} expired at {}",
                lease.epoch, lease.expires_at
            ),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn lease_expiry(now: DateTime<Utc>, ttl: Duration) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {
    if ttl.is_zero() {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "job lease ttl must be greater than zero".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    let delta = TimeDelta::from_std(ttl).map_err(|_| {
        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("job lease ttl is outside chrono range".to_string())
    })?;
    now.checked_add_signed(delta)
        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("job lease expiry overflow".to_string()))
}

fn lease_event(
    lease: &JobLease,
    sequence: JobEventSequence,
    disposition: LeaseClaimDisposition,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<JobEvent> {
    let mut detail = match serde_json::to_value(lease).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
        path: std::path::PathBuf::from("lease.json"),
        source,
    })? {
        Value::Object(detail) => detail,
        _ => Map::new(),
    };
    if let LeaseClaimDisposition::Reclaimed(reason) = disposition {
        detail.insert(
            "reclaim_reason".to_string(),
            Value::String(reason.as_str().to_string()),
        );
    }
    let event_id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
    Ok(JobEvent {
        schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
        job_id: lease.job_id.clone(),
        sequence,
        event_id,
        causation_id: format!(
            "lease-claim:{}:{}:{}",
            lease.job_id, lease.owner_id, lease.epoch
        ),
        timestamp: now,
        lease_epoch: lease.epoch,
        kind: match disposition {
            LeaseClaimDisposition::Acquired => JobEventKind::LeaseAcquired,
            LeaseClaimDisposition::Reclaimed(_) => JobEventKind::LeaseReclaimed,
        },
        detail: Value::Object(detail),
    })
}

fn lease_error(job_id: &JobId, detail: &str) -> DeadreckonError {
    DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("job lease {}: {detail}", job_id))
}

pub(crate) fn resolve_plan_owner(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    plan: &deadreckon_core::plan::Plan,
) -> Result<Option<ResolvedPlanOwner>> {
    let owner_job_id = plan.owner_job_id.clone().or_else(|| {
        paths
            .job_json(&plan.plan_id)
            .is_file()
            .then(|| plan.plan_id.clone())
    });
    let Some(owner_job_id) = owner_job_id else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let job = deadreckon_core::load_job(paths, &owner_job_id)?;
    if job.job_id.as_ref() != owner_job_id
        || !matches!(job.shape, JobShape::Graph | JobShape::LegacyCampaign)
    {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "Plan {} names incompatible durable Job {} as its owner",
            plan.plan_id, owner_job_id
        ))));
    }

    let mut lineage = Vec::new();
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut current = plan.clone();
    loop {
        if !seen.insert(current.plan_id.clone()) {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
                "Plan ownership lineage contains a cycle at {}",
                current.plan_id
            ))));
        }
        lineage.push(current.plan_id.clone());
        if lineage.len() as u32 > deadreckon_core::plan::MAX_SUBPLAN_DEPTH {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
                "Plan ownership lineage exceeds nesting cap {}",
                deadreckon_core::plan::MAX_SUBPLAN_DEPTH
            ))));
        }
        let compatible_owner = current.owner_job_id.as_deref() == Some(owner_job_id.as_str())
            || (current.owner_job_id.is_none() && current.plan_id == owner_job_id);
        if !compatible_owner {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
                "Plan {} does not retain durable Job owner {}",
                current.plan_id, owner_job_id
            ))));
        }
        let Some(parent_id) = current.parent_plan_id.as_deref() else {
            break;
        };
        let parent = deadreckon_core::load_plan(paths, parent_id)?;
        let reverse_links = parent
            .tasks
            .iter()
            .filter(|task| task.subplan.as_deref() == Some(current.plan_id.as_str())

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 07:46:02Z)**_

The cancellation concern is already covered by a stronger lower-level invariant: every fenced event reloads history while holding the per-Job control lock and suppresses non-cancellation events whenever cancellation is outstanding. I’ll add a direct regression test for that race, but no production workaround.

The restart defect is real. Its cause is the supervisor’s fallback ordering: durable `Failed + typed budget event` evidence is not classified unless child metadata still exists. I’m extending the existing merged-artifact restart checkpoint to recognize all durable advanced terminal evidence before the lost-containment fallback, and making budget finalization avoid duplicating `AttemptStopped` after a crash.

fn finish_advanced_budget_attempt(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: ChildExit,
    stop_reason: StopReason,
    artifact: &str,
    reason: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    if attempt_is_active(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())? {
        let projection = append_attempt_stopped(
            paths,
            token,
            stop_reason,
            json!({
                "exit": exit_detail(&exit),
                "artifact": artifact,
                "reason": reason,
            }),
        )?;
        if projection.stop_reason == Some(StopReason::CancelRequested) {
            finish_cancel_requested(paths, token, Some(&exit))?;
            return Ok(());
        }
    }
    append_terminal_event(
        paths,
        token,
        JobEventKind::BudgetExhausted,
        stop_reason,
        json!({
            "reason": reason,
            "artifact": artifact,
        }),
    )?;
    Ok(())
}

fn fail_advanced_attempt(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: ChildExit,
    reason: StopReason,
    message: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    )?;

fn finish_cancel_requested(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: Option<&ChildExit>,
) -> Result<bool> {
    let view = JobView::load(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())?;
    if view.projection.is_terminal() {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    if view.projection.stop_reason != Some(StopReason::CancelRequested) {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let attempt_active = attempt_is_active(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())?;
    if attempt_active {
        append_attempt_stopped(
            paths,
            token,
            StopReason::CancelRequested,
            json!({
                "reason": "operator cancelled the active durable attempt",
                "exit": exit.map(exit_detail),
            }),
        )?;
    }
    append_terminal_event(
        paths,
        token,
        JobEventKind::Cancelled,
        StopReason::CancelRequested,
        json!({
            "reason": if attempt_active {
                "operator cancelled the active durable attempt"
            } else {
                "operator cancelled before another attempt was launched"
            },
        }),
    )?;
    Ok(true)
}

fn attempt_is_active(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> Result<bool> {
    let history = read_job_history(&paths.job_events(token.job_id.as_ref()))?;

            JobEventKind::AttemptStopped => Some(false),
            JobEventKind::AttemptStarted => Some(true),
            _ => None,
        })
        .unwrap_or(false))
}

        }

name: operator-acceptance-checklist
description: Use when an implementation phase lands (or before declaring work done) — convert what was built into a concrete, plain-language manual test script the human runs from the operator's seat, instead of claiming completion yourself.
---

# Operator Acceptance Checklist

Completion is never the agent's to declare. At every phase boundary, translate the work into observable, operator-POV confirmation steps the human can execute by hand — which commands they can now run, what should look different, what to check. The human running those steps is the acceptance gate; the agent's report is not.

## Steps

1. At kickoff of any multi-phase build, establish the contract: "When there is something to build and test, stop and describe in plain language the functionality implemented, open questions, and exactly what to test."
2. When a phase is done, do NOT say "done" or just summarize the diff. Produce a manual test script.
3. The script must be operator-POV and concrete:
   - The exact commands to run (with working directory).
   - The new capability the user can now exercise end-to-end.
   - The specific, observable signal that confirms success (a journal/db entry, a UI change, a log line, a returned value).
   - What is explicitly NOT yet covered, so scope is honest.
4. Prefer real, runnable verification (a CLI invocation, a SQL/inspection command, a screen to open) over abstract description.
5. Hand the script to the user and wait — they verify by hand before the work is accepted.

## Verification

The deliverable of a phase is the test script itself. It passes the bar when a person who did not write the code could follow it start-to-finish and observe each success signal without asking a follow-up question.

## Failure modes

- Reporting "this should work" or pasting a diff as if it were acceptance. The user's response is "so what should i be able to test right now" / "explain clearly what I should be able to functionally test" — pre-empt it.
- Listing what changed in code terms instead of what the operator can now do and see.
- Omitting the not-yet-covered list, which hides scope and erodes trust in the checklist.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice in stoa (2025-10 → 2026-03), a recurrent and verified acceptance discipline. Consolidates the manual-test-script demand, operator-seat acceptance, and user-POV verification contract.

### 56.8 V1 boundaries

flag across verbs, giving campaigns a real scope (a schema change), `list --json`

namespacing, and a durable id index.

## 58. Watchkeeper: One Durable Job, Two-Key Completion

Watchkeeper adds a durable local Job above the existing run state. Guided
`start`, ordinary direct `run` and `orchestrate`, new chains, stored-plan
`fork`, and direct campaigns have one approved, queued, leased and supervised
parent Job ID. Every durable shape verifies a same-ID parent result with a
native deterministic gate and a fresh read-only semantic judge. The supervisor
validates the combined receipt before promotion. Explicit preview,
in-place/uncontained, historical chain, and continuation paths remain callable
process-owned compatibility paths.

### 58.1 Current execution boundary

| Entry path | Persistence and owner | Completion authority | Honest posture |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deadreckon start --mode run "<goal>"` | Writes a Job before the first turn, then detaches `supervisor serve --once <job-id>` | Contained native gate plus fresh read-only semantic `achieved`, sealed into one two-key receipt | Durable Single Job; survives the launching terminal |
| `start --mode review|full-plan` | Writes a `Graph` Job, normalizes delivery to `AtEnd`, and supervises the established conductor under the same parent ID | Copies the merged result into the same-ID parent run, then runs the native gate, fresh semantic judge, receipt validation and promotion | Durable and verified Graph parent; `finish` exports the receipt-bound parent |
| An auto-selected guided campaign | Writes a `LegacyCampaign` Job and supervises the established conductor under the same parent ID | Recovers exact persisted sub-plans, revalidates the worst-of roll-up, then runs the parent gate, semantic judge, receipt validation and promotion | Durable and verified Campaign parent; live recovery drills remain outstanding |
| Ordinary `deadreckon run "<goal>"` | Freezes direct-run options into a Single Job and detaches the same supervisor path | The same contained native gate, semantic judgment and combined receipt as guided Single | Durable by default; preview, explicit `--in-place`, explicit `--sandbox none`, and historical chain-child execution stay foreground and untrusted |
| Direct `orchestrate` and stored-plan `fork` | Freeze the graph into a `Graph` Job and supervise the established conductor under the parent lease | At-end same-ID parent gate, semantic judgment, receipt and promotion | Durable by default; preview and trusted internal child execution remain foreground |
| New `chain` | Compiles supported chain policy into a linear `Graph` Job | Verifies the composed parent once at the end with both completion keys | Durable by default; explicit `--sandbox none`, historical `chain run|resume`, and unsupported conductor-only policies remain labelled untrusted |
| Direct `campaign` | Writes a `LegacyCampaign` Job before the conductor starts | Rebuilds the worst-of roll-up, then uses the same parent two-key sequence | Durable by default; preview remains foreground and live recovery drills remain outstanding |
| Installed `deadreckon supervisor` user service | launchd or systemd starts `supervisor serve`, which scans supported nonterminal Jobs | Uses the same shape-specific classifiers and receipt validators as detached one-shot supervision | Conditional restart-at-login posture; live active-service and reboot acceptance remain |
| Guided automatic continuation | Refuses before creating a Job, run or worker | Prints the exact legacy `deadreckon extend <run-id> "<goal>"` command | Honest boundary until continuation shares the Job lifecycle |

Persisted durability and supervised durability are different claims. Every run
continues to write state, ledgers, snapshots, and evidence. A Watchkeeper Job
also has a renewable fenced owner, typed terminal reason, detached process
group, and immutable authority. Durable Single, Graph and Campaign Jobs also add
the combined parent completion receipt. Without the user service, the detached
supervisor can outlive its launching shell but is not a machine-restart
guarantee.

### 58.2 Job protocol, event history, and projection

`deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs` owns the checked schema-version-1 wire types:
`Job`, `JobEvent`, `JobLease`, `JobAuthority`, `SemanticJudgment`, and
`CompletionReceipt`. Job phase, terminal outcome, and causal `StopReason` are
separate enums, so `terminal` does not erase whether execution was verified,
cancelled, blocked, budget-exhausted, retry-exhausted, or stopped for review.

One Job is stored under:

```text
~/.deadreckon/jobs/<job-id>/
  job.json
  job-events.jsonl
  projection.json
  lease.json
  launch-plan.json
  acceptance.yam
... (truncated)
```

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 08:20:36Z)**_

The core system is now largely implemented. What remains is mainly real-world proof, one repair capability, and removal of compatibility complexity.

Since the loop began, we have created nine local commits on `main`; they are not pushed to `origin/main`. A further hardening tranche is implemented and fully tested but is still uncommitted.

## What we implemented

| Area | Current achievement |
|---|---|
| Durable job model | Added immutable job authority, append-only lifecycle events, fenced leases, attempt records, process ownership and recovery. |
| Detached execution | `start` creates a durable job, returns its ID and allows supervision to continue independently of the launching terminal. |
| Explicit stopping reasons | Jobs distinguish success, cancellation, blocking, failure, budget exhaustion and semantic uncertainty/revision. |
| Recovery | The supervisor can reclaim abandoned jobs, reject stale processes, recover incomplete launches and continue using the same parent ID. |
| Bounded execution | Attempt, wall-time and spend limits are persisted and enforced. Current hardening extends aggregate limits across plan tasks and campaign sub-plans. |
| Two-key completion | Deterministic checks must pass first. A fresh, read-only semantic judge must then return `achieved`. It can also return `revise` or `uncertain`. |
| Fail-closed judgment | A missing or invalid semantic judgment cannot produce an accepted result. It becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`. |
| Tamper-resistant receipts | HMAC-SHA-256 receipts bind the approved authority, contract, revisions, evidence and result tree. `finish` revalidates them before promotion. |
| Gate boundary | Signing material and protected evidence paths are withheld from agent execution. Synthetic provider “success” evidence is rejected. |
| One scheduler | Ordinary runs become Single Jobs; orchestration, stored plans and supported chains become Graph Jobs; campaigns become Campaign Jobs. |
| Parent verification | Graph and Campaign results are verified and receipted as one parent result rather than trusting individual children. |
| Service support | Commands and definitions exist for managed launchd/systemd supervision. |
| Operator surfaces | Job-aware `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list`, reports and `finish` read durable state rather than depending on an active UI. |
| Dogfood infrastructure | Added a 24-row trial matrix, metrics collector, result schemas and credential-free adversarial tampering tests. |

The current uncommitted tranche further adds:

- exact ownership between a Job and its Plan or Campaign;
- crash-safe reservation and launch of campaign sub-plans;
- same-ID repair when intermediate mapping files disappear;
- aggregate planner and child budget accounting;
- recovery of persisted typed budget outcomes;
- cancellation winning cleanly during terminal classification;
- isolation of historical chain/orchestration characterization behind a separate feature-gated binary.

The complete verification gate passed, including formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, 790 main CLI tests, all workspace integration suites, feature-gated chain/orchestration suites and an optimized release build. The final independent audit found no blocking issue.

## What is still on the docket

### 1. Commit the current hardening tranche

It is ready for a carefully scoped local commit. It touches 29 tracked files plus one new ownership test. User-owned `.specstory`, editor and unrelated documentation changes must remain excluded.

### 2. Prove the promise using real work

This is now the largest gap. The dogfood kit currently records only two unsuccessful attempts, 22 unrun rows and zero live verified completions.

We still need to run 20–30 genuine tasks across:

- at least two repositories;
- multiple real provider routes;
- different task shapes and definitions of done;
- terminal, worker and supervisor termination;
- network loss and restoration;
- tampering attempts;
- a real login or machine reboot.

Then calculate intervention rates, recovery rates, false acceptance/rejection, time, spend and judging cost. The existing checklist describes this in [WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md:380).

### 3. Add safe semantic repair for Graph and Campaign jobs

A Single Job can respond to semantic `revise` and try bounded corrective work. Graph and Campaign parents currently stop at `NEEDS_REVIEW`. They need a controlled repair path that preserves the original authority and receipt boundary.

### 4. Validate the user service for real

The launchd/systemd definitions and commands are implemented and hermetically tested. We have not yet demonstrated an installed service reclaiming work after an actual logout, login or reboot.

### 5. Finish provider and containment parity

Strict paths fail closed, but provider adapters do not all offer equivalent structured events, spend accounting or sandbox behavior. Subscription quotas and universal usage accounting remain incomplete.

### 6. Retire compatibility complexity

Historical `chain run|resume`, preview modes, unsupported conductor policies and some legacy run-oriented projections remain. Once the durable paths survive dogfooding, these should either be translated honestly onto Jobs or explicitly retired.

## The honest assessment

We have built most of the necessary machinery behind the desired statement:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify both the checks and the meaning of the result, and leave behind a clear receipt explaining what happened.

The code now supports that claim structurally and under extensive automated fault tests. We cannot yet make it as a fully demonstrated product claim because the live cross-provider, active-service, reboot and 20–30-task trials have not happened.

The correct next move is therefore to commit the completed hardening, freeze further feature expansion, and spend the next phase trying to break DeadReckon on real work. The current architectural status is also summarized in [MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md:84).

Accept when all are true:

- [ ] `start.json` contains one ID under `dispatched.ids`.
- [ ] `job-view.json` ends with phase `terminal`, outcome `verified`, and stop

- [ ] `receipt.json` names the same Job and run ID.

- [ ] authority, contract, marker, semantic judgment, result-tree and signature
  digests are present.
- [ ] `finish` succeeded only after the receipt existed.

```

Record the ID, then close that terminal without running `kill`. In a new
terminal, restore `WK_BIN`, `WK_REPO_A`, `WK_STATE`, `WK_JOB_ID`, and:

```bash
export DEADRECKON_HOME="$WK_STATE"
cd "$WK_REPO_A"
"$WK_BIN" status "$WK_JOB_ID" --plain --json
"$WK_BIN" attach "$WK_JOB_ID"
```

Accept when:

- [ ] the Job continued after the launching shell disappeared;
- [ ] status and attach use the same parent ID;
- [ ] leaving attach does not cancel the Job;
- [ ] a terminal state has a typed outcome and stop reason.

This proves process detachment, not machine-restart recovery.

## 3. Kill and reclaim the supervisor

pub(crate) async fn done_command(
    args: Vec<String>,
    provider: Option<String>,
    model: Option<String>,
    force: bool,
    spec: Option<PathBuf>,
    against: Option<PathBuf>,
) -> Result<()> {
    let Some(first) = args.first().map(String::as_str) else {
        return acceptance_explain_command(spec);
    };
    match first {
        "add" => {
            let request = args.iter().skip(1).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();
            if request.is_empty() {
                return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
                    "done add needs a criterion",
                    "deadreckon def-done add \"users can save drawings\"",
                )));
            }
            acceptance_add_command(request, provider, model, force).await
        }
        "check" => acceptance_check_command(spec, against),
        "show" | "explain" => acceptance_explain_command(spec),
        "edit" | "refine" => {
            let request = args.iter().skip(1).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();
            if request.is_empty() {
                return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
                    "done edit needs a requested change",
                    "deadreckon def-done edit \"also require the gallery to persist\"",
                )));
            }
            acceptance_agent_command(
                AcceptanceAgentMode::Refine,
                request,
                None,
                provider,
                model,
                force,
            )
            .await
        }
        "help" => {
            print_done_help();
            Ok(())
        }
        _ => {
            acceptance_agent_command(
                AcceptanceAgentMode::Draft,
                args,
                None,
                provider,
                model,
                true,
            )
            .await
        }
    }
}

fn print_done_help() {
    println!("{}", ui_heading("deadreckon def-done"));
    println!("{}", ui_muted("usage:"));
    println!(
        "  {}",
        ui_command("deadreckon def-done \"builds, opens in a browser, and has no console errors\"")
    );
    println!(
        "  {}",
        ui_command("deadreckon def-done add \"users can save drawings\"")
    );
    println!("  {}", ui_command("deadreckon def-done check"));
    println!("  {}", ui_command("deadreckon def-done show"));
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum AcceptanceAgentMode {
    Draft,
    Refine,
}

fn acceptance_init_command(preset: AcceptancePreset, force: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
    let preset = match preset {
        AcceptancePreset::Auto => detect_acceptance_preset(&cwd),
        other => other,
    };
    let draft = acceptance_template_for_preset(preset, &cwd);
    write_project_acceptance(&cwd, &draft, force, false)?;
    print_acceptance_written(&cwd, "template", acceptance_check_count(&draft.yaml)?);
    let compiled = compile_contract_with_source(
        &draft.yaml,
        Some(&draft.markdown),
        project_acceptance_yaml(&cwd),
    )?;
    println!("{}", ui_heading("compiled done contract"));
    print_compiled_contract(&compiled, None);
