---
name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
---

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

Before editing, you should be able to answer, in writing: "The behavior is produced by `<file>:<lines>` because `<causal chain>`, and I will confirm the fix by `<observation/command>`." If you cannot, you have not finished diagnosing.

## Failure modes

- Patching the layer where the symptom appears (e.g. button-state code) when the real cause is elsewhere (a default selection upstream). The user rejects this with: "You got it wrong… the issue was not with the button states." Localize first.
- Jumping to a fix on the first plausible theory. Demand or construct the observation that would discriminate between candidate causes before committing to one.
- Editing during a "don't write any code yet" instruction. That instruction is a gate, not a delay — produce the mechanism trace and stop.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-04), consistently followed by the user, high adjacent-approval rate. Consolidates the read-before-write gate, fault-localization-before-fix, and mechanism-trace-before-trust patterns.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 08:32:23Z)**_

Diagnosis is now pinned before any edit:

- The semantic judge intentionally sends a fresh request with `session_dir: None` and `output_path: None` in `semantic_judge.rs`.
- The Codex adapter only writes `--output-schema` when a session directory exists, and only adds `-o/--output-last-message` when an output path exists in `cli_codex.rs`.
- This installed Codex supports both flags, but neither was passed. The adapter therefore returned Codex’s JSONL event stream; the semantic parser read the first `{"type": ...}` event as the judgment and rejected it.
- Verification will require adapter tests for fresh read-only structured requests plus a repeat of the real public Job reaching a persisted semantic judgment, valid receipt, and successful `finish`.

That is the production cause, not a judging-policy problem. The existing loop authorization covers correcting defects exposed by dogfooding, so I’m proceeding at the provider adapter layer.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 09:01:55Z)**_

The core promise now works end to end, but the loop is not finished. We have moved from “design and scaffolding” to “one genuinely verified live result.” What remains is hardening, broader interruption testing, and simplifying the surrounding product.

## What we implemented

| Area | Current achievement |
|---|---|
| Durable Job model | Added immutable authority, Job identity, append-only lifecycle events, leases, retry policy, deadlines, budgets, semantic judgments and completion receipts. |
| Detached execution | `start` creates the Job before execution, returns its ID and lets a supervisor continue independently of the launching terminal. |
| Recovery | Added lease reclaim, process-group supervision, crash-atomic child launch, same-ID recovery and reconstruction of persisted Graph/Campaign work. |
| Typed stopping | Jobs distinguish `verified`, `needs_review`, `blocked`, `budget_exhausted`, `deadline_reached`, `retry_exhausted`, `cancelled` and `failed`, with specific causal stop reasons. |
| One Job scheduler | Ordinary single runs, orchestration/plans, new supported chains, stored-plan forks and campaigns now execute beneath a durable parent Job. |
| Deterministic verification | Approved definitions of done run inside a resolved sandbox. A failed deterministic check can never be overruled by an LLM. |
| Semantic second key | After checks pass, a fresh read-only judge assesses the goal, contract, diff and evidence as `achieved`, `revise` or `uncertain`. Unavailable or malformed judging fails closed as `NEEDS_REVIEW`. |
| Signed receipts | Completion receipts use HMAC-SHA-256 and bind the authority, approved contract, policy, launch plan, source/result revisions, deterministic proof, semantic judgment, containment and result-tree digest. |
| Gate isolation | Signing keys live outside the agent workspace. Gate, proof, Job and authority paths are denied or read-only across supported sandbox/provider routes. |
| Deliberate promotion | `finish` revalidates the complete receipt and current result before applying it to the source repository. |
| Operator surface | Jobs are resolved through `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list` and `finish`; reports and views derive from durable state. |
| Dogfood infrastructure | Added a 24-row operator kit, adversarial runner, metrics collector, schemas and the [operator acceptance checklist](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md:1). |

This work is represented by ten local commits, from `79bb2e8` through `dce5e06`: approximately 36,000 inserted lines across 129 tracked files.

## What we have actually proven

We have now completed one real Codex-backed journey:

1. An approved definition of done initially failed.
2. `start` returned one detached Job ID.
3. Codex changed the isolated worktree.
4. The deterministic Cargo checks passed.
5. An independent read-only Codex judgment returned `achieved` with evidence-backed goal coverage.
6. DeadReckon created a valid, contained, two-key HMAC receipt.
7. Changing the receipt signature caused `finish` to refuse promotion.
8. Restoring the original receipt allowed `finish` to apply the result.
9. The resulting repository test passed and produced the requested output.

That is the first live demonstration of the intended sentence:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It works in isolation, independently verifies both the checks and the meaning, and leaves a receipt explaining what happened.

The credential-free adversarial runner also recorded 7 passes, 0 failures and 5 explicitly unproven scenarios.

## Implemented, but not sufficiently proven yet

- Graph and Campaign Jobs can recover persisted ownership, budgets and mappings, but have not completed the full live interruption matrix.
- Supervisor service definitions exist for launchd and systemd, but machine-reboot recovery has not been demonstrated.
- Single Jobs can act on semantic `revise`; Graph and Campaign parents currently stop for review because safe parent repair is not implemented.
- Gate forgery, receipt mutation and protected-path attacks have strong automated coverage, but hostile cross-provider trials remain.
- Provider routes share the outer contract, but structured events, usage reporting and steering are uneven.
- Subscription-backed provider usage is not truly bounded by a dollar cap. One tiny live task reported more than 200,000 input tokens while recording $0.
- Narration and documentation work currently adds substantial latency and noise.

## Immediate defects found by dogfooding

These should be fixed before calling the tranche merge-ready.

1. The Codex semantic-judge adapter

The first live job failed closed because Codex JSONL transport events were passed to the semantic parser instead of the final structured answer. A four-file adapter fix is implemented, tested and was used successfully in the second live job, but it remains uncommitted.

2. Cleanup reports success when it failed

`finish --cleanup` applied the verified result, but a dirty worktree prevented removal. DeadReckon discarded both Git errors, claimed cleanup was complete and left the worktree and branch behind.

The fix must report “applied; cleanup incomplete,” preserve the successful delivery, verify removal postconditions, and support cleanup of a Job’s same-ID backing Run. It must not silently force-delete untracked evidence. The cause is in [lifecycle.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/lifecycle.rs:1225).

3. Provider-private files leaked into the delivered result

SpecStory created `.specstory/**` files inside the writable worktree. DeadReckon treated every filesystem change as deliverable, staged with `git add -A`, signed those files into the result digest and promoted them.

We need one shared artifact policy used by:

- turn staging;
- semantic evidence;
- receipt hashing;
- finish preview and application.

Provider telemetry such as `.specstory/**` should remain private run evidence unless the approved contract explicitly allows it. The generated `docs/RUN-*` files and implementation notes are intentional under today’s contract, although their default cost and volume deserve a later product decision.

## What remains on the main docket

In priority order:

1. Land the semantic adapter, cleanup and artifact-boundary fixes with regression tests.
2. Run the full `make verify` and commit that hardening tranche.
3. Complete the 20–30-task dogfood campaign across two repositories and at least two providers.
4. Kill live provider workers and supervisors and prove same-ID recovery without duplicate execution.
5. Test network loss and restoration.
6. Prove restart-after-login and machine-reboot recovery using another OS user or VM. The current fixed launchd identity cannot safely isolate a disposable service using only `DEADRECKON_HOME`.
7. Add safe semantic-revise repair for Graph and Campaign parents.
8. Measure false acceptance, false rejection, operator interventions, comprehension time and judging/supervision cost.
9. Fix subscription quota accounting and make optional narration unable to dominate a small coding task.
10. Retire or quarantine legacy chain, preview, in-place and uncontained compatibility paths rather than maintaining two lifecycle models.
11. Freeze deeper campaign, learning and narration expansion until the durable core has enough real usage evidence.

## Repository state

The ten completed commits are on local `main`, which is ten commits ahead of `origin/main`. They have not been pushed. The Codex adapter fix is still an uncommitted four-file change. User-owned `.specstory`, editor and documentation changes remain separate and have not been incorporated into the Watchkeeper commits.

So the honest assessment is: the differentiated Job kernel is substantially built and has succeeded once under live conditions. The remaining work is no longer “invent the architecture”; it is “remove the defects dogfooding exposed, prove interruption recovery repeatedly, measure trustworthiness, and prune the incidental complexity.”

+#[test]
+fn dirty_finish_cleanup_reports_incomplete_and_same_id_job_cleanup_recovers() {
+    let temp = repo_tempdir();
+    let repo = clean_git_repo(&temp);
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
+    let run_id = run_worktree_smoke(&paths, &repo);
+    let state = load_run(&paths, &run_id).expect("state");
+    let record = read_codebase_record(&state.working_dir).expect("codebase");
+    let worktree = record.worktree_path.clone().expect("worktree");
+    let branch = record.branch_name.clone().expect("branch");
+    let private_history = worktree.join(".specstory/history/narrator.md");
+    fs::create_dir_all(private_history.parent().expect("history parent")).expect("history dir");
+    fs::write(&private_history, "untracked provider evidence\n").expect("private history");
+
+    let apply = deadreckon(&paths)
+        .current_dir(&repo)
+        .arg("apply")
+        .arg(&run_id)
+        .arg("--no-confirm")
+        .arg("--cleanup")
+        .output()
+        .expect("apply");
+
+    assert!(
+        !apply.status.success(),
+        "dirty cleanup must not report success:\n{}",
+        stdout(&apply)
+    );
+    let stderr = stderr(&apply);
+    assert!(stderr.contains("applied"), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(stderr.contains("cleanup did not complete"), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(
+        stderr.contains(&format!("deadreckon cleanup {} --overwrite", &run_id[..8])),
+        "{stderr}"
+    );
+    assert!(worktree.exists());
+    assert!(git_ref_exists(&repo, &branch));
+    assert!(!state.run_root.join("abandoned.json").exists());
+    assert!(
+        git_stdout(&repo, &["diff", "--stat", &format!("HEAD..{branch}")])
+            .trim()
+            .is_empty(),
+        "apply must remain successful even though cleanup failed"
+    );
+
+    write_same_id_job(&paths, &state, &repo);
+    let cleanup = deadreckon(&paths)
+        .current_dir(&repo)
+        .arg("cleanup")
+        .arg(&run_id)
+        .arg("--overwrite")
+        .output()
+        .expect("same-id Job cleanup");
+
+    assert_success(&cleanup);
+    assert!(!worktree.exists());
+    assert!(!git_ref_exists(&repo, &branch));
+    assert!(state.run_root.join("abandoned.json").exists());
+}

+fn write_same_id_job(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
+    repo: &std::path::Path,
+) {
+    let job_id = JobId(state.run_id.clone());
+    let job = Job {
+        schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
+        job_id: job_id.clone(),
+        scope: state.scope.clone(),
+        goal: state.goal.clone(),
+        shape: JobShape::Single,
+        created_at: Utc::now(),
+        source_cwd: repo.to_path_buf(),
+        launch_plan_sha256: "sha256:test-launch".to_string(),
+        authority_sha256: "sha256:test-authority".to_string(),
+        policy: JobPolicy {
+            max_spend_usd: 1.0,
+            max_wall_seconds: 60,
+            max_attempts: 1,
+            deadline: None,
+            semantic_judge: SemanticJudgeMode::Required,
+        },
+    };
+    write_job(paths, &job).expect("job");
+    append_job_event(
+        paths,
+        &JobEvent {
+            schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
+            job_id,
+            sequence: JobEventSequence::new(1).expect("nonzero"),
+            event_id: "created".to_string(),
+            causation_id: "created".to_string(),
+            timestamp: Utc::now(),
+            lease_epoch: 0,
+            kind: JobEventKind::Created,
+            detail: serde_json::json!({}),
+        },
+    )
+    .expect("created event");
+}

+fn resolve_cleanup_state(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    reference: &str,
+) -> Result<deadreckon_core::PipelineState> {
+    match super::reference::resolve_ref(
+        paths,
+        super::reference::RefQuery {
+            reference: Some(reference),
+            all_scopes: false,
+            verb: "cleanup",
+        },
+    )? {
+        super::reference::ResolvedRef::Job(job) => {
+            load_run(paths, job.job.job_id.as_ref()).map_err(|source| {
+                CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
+                    &format!(
+                        "job {} has no recoverable same-ID run workspace: {source}",
+                        job.job.job_id
+                    ),
+                    &format!("deadreckon show {}", run_prefix(job.job.job_id.as_ref())),
+                ))
+            })
+        }
+        super::reference::ResolvedRef::Run(state)
+        | super::reference::ResolvedRef::PlanChild { state, .. } => Ok(*state),
+        other => Err(super::reference::refusal_for(
+            other.kind(),
+            "cleanup",
+            &super::reference::resolved_id(&other),
+        )),
+    }
+}

+fn git_worktree_registered(git_root: &Path, worktree: &Path) -> Result<bool> {
+    let listing = git_stdout(git_root, &["worktree", "list", "--porcelain"])?;
+    Ok(listing.lines().any(|line| {
+        line.strip_prefix("worktree ")
+            .is_some_and(|path| Path::new(path) == worktree)
+    }))
+}
+
+fn local_branch_exists(git_root: &Path, branch: &str) -> Result<bool> {
+    let reference = format!("refs/heads/{branch}");
+    let output =
+        deadreckon_core::git::run_git(git_root, &["show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", &reference])?;
+    Ok(output.status.success())
+}
+
+fn cleanup_incomplete_error(
+    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
+    record: &CodebaseRecord,
+    reason: CleanupReason,
+    force: bool,
+    removed: &[String],
+    detail: &str,
+) -> CliError {
+    let id = run_prefix(&state.run_id);
+    let mut evidence = vec![
+        ("run".to_string(), id.clone()),
+        ("cleanup".to_string(), "incomplete".to_string()),
+        ("failure".to_string(), one_line(detail, 240)),
+        ("removed entries".to_string(), removed.len().to_string()),
+    ];
+    for (index, item) in removed.iter().enumerate() {
+        evidence.push((format!("removed {}", index + 1), item.clone()));
+    }
+    if let Some(worktree) = record.worktree_path.as_ref()
+        && worktree.exists()
+    {
+        evidence.push(("retained worktree".to_string(), worktree.display().to_string()));
+    }
+    if let Some(branch) = record.branch_name.as_ref() {
+        evidence.push(("retained branch".to_string(), branch.clone()));
+    }
+    let what = match reason {
+        CleanupReason::Applied => {
+            "DeadReckon applied the run, but cleanup did not complete."
+        }
+        CleanupReason::Abandoned => {
+            "DeadReckon could not finish removing the abandoned run resources."
+        }
+        CleanupReason::Cleaned => {
+            "DeadReckon could not finish removing the selected run resources."
+        }
+    };
+    let why = "Git refused or failed a cleanup operation. DeadReckon retained the remaining resources, did not write a completed-cleanup marker, and requires explicit overwrite authority before discarding untracked evidence.";
+    let recommended = if force {
+        format!("deadreckon show {id}")
+    } else {
+        format!("deadreckon cleanup {id} --overwrite")
+    };
+    CliError::Surface {
+        code: 1,
+        surface: VerdictSurface::must_new(
+            VerdictKind::Blocked,
+            reason.subject(),
+            Some(&id),
+            ExplanationPanel::new(what, why, evidence),
+            vec![("Recommended", recommended)],
+            vec![("Secondary", format!("deadreckon show {id}"))],
+        )
+        .render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false)),
+    }
+}

+/// One policy for classifying paths inside an agent-visible working tree.
+///
+/// Evidence-only paths are retained in run evidence but must never affect the
+/// semantic diff, signed deliverable tree, result commit, or promoted output.
+/// Ignored paths are neither deliverables nor useful run evidence.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum ArtifactDisposition {
+    Deliverable,
+    EvidenceOnly,
+    Ignored,
+}
+
+const EVIDENCE_ONLY_ROOTS: [&str; 1] = [".specstory"];
+
+pub const fn evidence_only_roots() -> &'static [&'static str] {
+    &EVIDENCE_ONLY_ROOTS
+}
+
+pub fn classify_artifact_path(path: &Path) -> ArtifactDisposition {
+    let mut evidence_only = false;
+    for component in path.components() {
+        let Component::Normal(name) = component else {
+            continue;
+        };
+        if matches!(
+            name.to_string_lossy().as_ref(),
+            ".git" | ".deadreckon" | "target" | "node_modules"
+        ) {
+            return ArtifactDisposition::Ignored;
+        }
+        if EVIDENCE_ONLY_ROOTS
+            .iter()
+            .any(|root| name == std::ffi::OsStr::new(root))
+        {
+            evidence_only = true;
+        }
+    }
+    if evidence_only {
+        ArtifactDisposition::EvidenceOnly
+    } else {
+        ArtifactDisposition::Deliverable
+    }
+}
+
+pub fn is_deliverable_artifact_path(path: &Path) -> bool {
+    classify_artifact_path(path) == ArtifactDisposition::Deliverable
+}
+

+pub fn copy_deliverable_tree(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> Result<()> {
+    fs::create_dir_all(to).with_path(to)?;
+    if !from.exists() {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    for entry in WalkDir::new(from).into_iter().filter_entry(|entry| {
+        entry
+            .path()
+            .strip_prefix(from)
+            .ok()
+            .is_none_or(|relative| {
+                relative.as_os_str().is_empty() || is_deliverable_artifact_path(relative)
+            })
+    }) {
+        let entry = entry.map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
+            path: from.to_path_buf(),
+            source: source.into(),
+        })?;
+        let relative = entry.path().strip_prefix(from).map_err(|err| {
+            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("copy source prefix error: {err}"))
+        })?;
+        if relative.as_os_str().is_empty() {
+            continue;
+        }
+        let target = to.join(relative);
+        if entry.file_type().is_dir() {
+            fs::create_dir_all(&target).with_path(&target)?;
+        } else if entry.file_type().is_file() {
+            if let Some(parent) = target.parent() {
+                fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
+            }
+            fs::copy(entry.path(), &target).with_path(&target)?;
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}

+//! Shared classification for paths inside an agent-visible workspace.
+
+use std::path::{Component, Path};
+
+/// Whether a workspace path belongs in the operator's result or only in
+/// DeadReckon's private evidence/control state.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum WorkspacePathClass {
+    Deliverable,
+    EvidenceOnly,
+    LifecycleMetadata,
+    RuntimeOnly,
+}
+
+const EVIDENCE_ONLY_ROOTS: [&str; 1] = [".specstory"];
+
+pub const fn evidence_only_roots() -> &'static [&'static str] {
+    &EVIDENCE_ONLY_ROOTS
+}
+
+pub fn classify_workspace_path(path: &Path) -> WorkspacePathClass {
+    let mut evidence_only = false;
+    for component in path.components() {
+        let Component::Normal(name) = component else {
+            continue;
+        };
+        if matches!(
+            name.to_string_lossy().as_ref(),
+            ".git" | "target" | "node_modules"
+        ) {
+            return WorkspacePathClass::RuntimeOnly;
+        }
+        if name == ".deadreckon" {
+            return WorkspacePathClass::LifecycleMetadata;
+        }
+        if EVIDENCE_ONLY_ROOTS
+            .iter()
+            .any(|root| name == std::ffi::OsStr::new(root))
+        {
+            evidence_only = true;
+        }
+    }
+    if evidence_only {
+        WorkspacePathClass::EvidenceOnly
+    } else {
+        WorkspacePathClass::Deliverable
+    }
+}
+
+pub fn is_deliverable_workspace_path(path: &Path) -> bool {
+    classify_workspace_path(path) == WorkspacePathClass::Deliverable
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use std::path::Path;
+
+    use super::{WorkspacePathClass, classify_workspace_path};
+
+    #[test]
+    fn specstory_is_evidence_only_while_run_docs_and_notes_are_deliverable() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            classify_workspace_path(Path::new(".specstory/history/session.md")),
+            WorkspacePathClass::EvidenceOnly
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            classify_workspace_path(Path::new("docs/RUN-AS-BUILT.md")),
+            WorkspacePathClass::Deliverable
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            classify_workspace_path(Path::new("implementation-notes.html")),
+            WorkspacePathClass::Deliverable
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            classify_workspace_path(Path::new(".deadreckon/codebase.json")),
+            WorkspacePathClass::LifecycleMetadata
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            classify_workspace_path(Path::new("target/debug/deadreckon")),
+            WorkspacePathClass::RuntimeOnly
+        );
+    }
+}
```

+/// Hash only paths eligible to cross the verified result boundary.
+///
+/// The broad working index remains the flight/checkpoint primitive so private
+/// provider evidence is recoverable. Authority, semantic, receipt and

+    index
+        .files
+        .retain(|path, _| is_deliverable_workspace_path(path));
+    Ok(index)
+}

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 09:48:57Z)**_

The short version: we have built most of the new execution engine, but we have not yet earned the full reliability claim through broad real-world testing.

All completed work is currently committed directly to local `main`, which is 12 commits ahead of `origin/main`. Nothing has been pushed. One additional security-boundary tranche is still uncommitted.

| Original initiative | Current state |
|---|---|
| Durable goal executor | Mostly implemented |
| Semantic meta-judge | Implemented and proven once with real Codex |
| Protected gate and receipts | Implemented; final artifact boundary still being hardened |
| One Job model | Implemented for new execution; legacy models still exist internally |
| Dogfood 20–30 tasks | Harness built, execution largely outstanding |

## What we have implemented

### 1. Durable detached Jobs

`deadreckon start` can now create a durable Job, return its ID, and run it detached.

The implementation includes:

- append-only Job lifecycle events;
- fenced leases and heartbeats;
- abandoned-lease recovery;
- supervisor restart and worker adoption;
- bounded attempts, spend and wall time;
- explicit terminal outcomes including completed, blocked, cancelled, failed, budget-exhausted and needs-review;
- PID and process-start identity to avoid adopting the wrong process;
- crash-atomic worker launching, so a crash between “starting” and “running” does not silently duplicate work;
- service-oriented supervision;
- same-ID ownership between the Job and its underlying run or plan.

This is the largest completed part of the work.

### 2. Runs, chains, plans and campaigns on the Job scheduler

Ordinary direct runs, supported chains, graphs, nested plans and campaigns now enter through the durable Job scheduler.

We also added:

- recovery of partially created parent/child relationships;
- recovery of reserved but not fully launched child work;
- aggregate parent and child spend/time limits;
- cancellation precedence during recovery;
- parent verification and receipt handling.

This is functional convergence. It is not yet a total removal of the older Run, Chain and Plan representations. Those remain for compatibility and internal execution.

### 3. Two-key completion

A successful Job now requires both:

1. Deterministic definition-of-done checks.
2. An independent, read-only semantic judgment.

The semantic judge receives the goal, approved contract, result diff and evidence. It returns an evidence-backed result such as achieved, revise or uncertain.

Important constraints are in place:

- semantic judgment cannot override a failed deterministic check;
- malformed or unsupported evidence is rejected;
- judging is budget-aware;
- synthetic completion evidence is rejected;
- unavailable semantic judging produces `needs_review`, rather than silently accepting the result.

A real Codex dogfood run initially exposed an adapter bug: Codex’s JSONL event stream was being parsed instead of its structured final judgment. That has been fixed and committed.

### 4. Protected receipts and gate authority

We now have HMAC-authenticated completion receipts that bind the result to its authority and verification evidence.

Implemented protections include:

- signing material outside the agent-visible workspace;
- protected gate paths;
- HMAC receipt authentication;
- source-authority binding;
- contract and policy binding;
- result revision and tree identity;
- deterministic and semantic evidence;
- refusal of corrupted, malformed, forged or over-budget evidence;
- validation before promotion or delivery.

In the real Codex run, the valid receipt was accepted, an altered signature was refused, and restoring the valid receipt allowed `finish` to apply the result.

### 5. Operator lifecycle

The ordinary surface now centres on:

```text
start
attach
status
list
finish
```

Jobs can be inspected through the same identity, and verified results can be promoted and delivered.

A live run exposed another bug: applying the result succeeded, but dirty-worktree cleanup failed while DeadReckon reported that it succeeded. That is now fixed:

- cleanup errors are no longer discarded;
- actual worktree and branch postconditions are checked;
- delivery remains recorded if apply succeeded;
- the outcome says “applied, cleanup incomplete”;
- explicit same-ID Job cleanup can recover the retained run;
- forceful deletion still requires explicit operator authority.

### 6. Documentation and adversarial infrastructure

We added:

- the durable execution goal and protocol;
- the operator contract;
- acceptance instructions;
- a 24-task, multi-repository/provider dogfood matrix;
- metrics collection;
- credential-free crash, evidence and tamper trials;
- recovery-boundary tests.

The credential-free adversarial suite currently records:

- 7 passed;
- 0 failed;
- 5 explicitly unproven.

Those unproven claims require real host or provider conditions and have not been converted into pretend test successes.

## What is currently being built

The live Codex run uncovered a third issue: provider-private `.specstory` files entered the result worktree and therefore affected parts of the signed and delivered result.

The uncommitted tranche introduces one central artifact classification:

- deliverable;
- evidence-only;
- lifecycle metadata;
- runtime-only.

The intended rule is:

- provider-private artifacts such as `.specstory/**` may remain in raw provenance;
- they must not count as product progress;
- they must not enter semantic diffs;
- they must not be committed to the result;
- they must not affect the deliverable receipt;
- they must not enter promoted libraries, parent plans or campaigns;
- `finish` must refuse a legacy result containing those files.

This work currently touches 14 source files and is not yet committed or fully verified.

## What remains on the docket

### Immediate engineering work

1. Finish the provider-private artifact boundary.
2. Ensure turn staging cannot accidentally commit evidence-only files.
3. Require every deliverable change to be committed before sealing a receipt.
4. Make `finish` prove that the delivered result matches the signed result.
5. Cover plan, graph, campaign, promotion and crash-recovery paths with the same classifier.
6. Run focused tests, Clippy and the complete repository verification gate.
7. Commit that tranche separately.

### Immediate proof work

1. Repeat the real Codex Job after the three discovered bugs are fixed.
2. Confirm `.specstory` remains provenance but never enters the delivered result.
3. Kill the worker and confirm recovery.
4. Kill the supervisor and confirm adoption or bounded retry.
5. Exercise cancellation and budget exhaustion.
6. Remove network access and verify a truthful bounded outcome.
7. Attempt gate and receipt tampering again.
8. Run a hostile second provider route.

### Broader dogfooding

The checked-in matrix has 24 tasks:

- 2 attempted;
- 22 not run;
- 0 recorded as verified in the sanitized matrix.

The separate disposable Codex run did reach verified completion, but it has not yet been sanitized into a formal matrix result because it exposed the artifact-boundary defect.

We still need the 20–30 real-task campaign across multiple repositories and providers, followed by measurements of:

- unattended completion;
- recovery;
- false acceptance;
- false rejection;
- operator interventions;
- understanding time;
- supervision and judging cost.

## Honest overall assessment

The architecture now expresses the intended product. This is no longer merely a proposal or thin scaffolding.

However:

- the durable execution engine is largely built;
- the two-key gate and protected receipt work in a real happy-path run;
- recovery has extensive automated coverage;
- one full live run has succeeded;
- broad host/provider recovery has not been demonstrated;
- the 24-task proof campaign is still mostly outstanding;
- the artifact/result identity boundary is still actively being closed.

So the destination statement is now a credible description of the design, but not yet a fully demonstrated product guarantee:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify both the checks and the meaning of the result, and leave behind a clear receipt explaining what happened.

The shortest path from here is: finish the artifact boundary, pass the full verification gate, rerun the successful Codex journey, and then concentrate almost entirely on destructive dogfooding rather than adding more features.

+fn restore_evidence_only_candidate_paths(worktree: &Path, base_commit: &str) -> Result<()> {
+    for root in deadreckon_core::evidence_only_roots() {
+        let path = worktree.join(root);
+        remove_if_exists(&path)?;
+        let base_files =
+            git_stdout(worktree, &["ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", base_commit, "--", root])?;
+        if base_files.trim().is_empty() {
+            // The provider may have committed this private path itself. Stage
+            // its deletion so the candidate branch converges back to the
+            // approved base even though the broad delivery add excludes it.
+            run_git(worktree, &["add", "-A", "--", root])?;
+        } else {
+            run_git(
+                worktree,
+                &[
+                    "restore",
+                    "--source",
+                    base_commit,
+                    "--staged",
+                    "--worktree",
+                    "--",
+                    root,
+                ],
+            )?;
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}

+/// Persist the lifecycle routing record outside the agent-visible workspace.
+///
+/// The workspace copy remains useful to docs and legacy commands, but delivery
+/// and receipt code should prefer this control-plane copy so a provider cannot
+/// redirect `finish` by editing `.deadreckon/codebase.json`.
+pub fn write_trusted_codebase_record(run_root: &Path, record: &CodebaseRecord) -> Result<()> {
+    let path = run_root.join(TRUSTED_CODEBASE_RECORD);
+    std::fs::write(
+        &path,
+        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(record).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
+            path: path.clone(),
+            source,
+        })?,
+    )
+    .with_path(path)
+}
+
+pub fn read_trusted_codebase_record(run_root: &Path) -> Result<CodebaseRecord> {
+    let path = run_root.join(TRUSTED_CODEBASE_RECORD);
+    let data = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
+    serde_json::from_slice(&data).with_json_path(path)
+}
+
+pub fn read_run_codebase_record(run_root: &Path, working_dir: &Path) -> Result<CodebaseRecord> {
+    read_trusted_codebase_record(run_root).or_else(|error| {
+        if matches!(
+            &error,
+            DeadreckonError::Io { source, .. }
+                if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound
+        ) {
+            read_codebase_record(working_dir)
+        } else {
+            Err(error)
+        }
+    })
+}

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 10:16:16Z)**_

## Current position

We have built most of the product spine. We have not yet proved the full promise safely enough for unattended use.

We are now in the hardening and acceptance phase, not the main feature-building phase.

| Original workstream | Current state |
|---|---|
| durable goal executor | implemented, but machine and crash recovery still need live proof |
| semantic meta-judge | implemented and exercised successfully |
| secure gate and receipt | implemented, but the current audit found boundary problems that must be fixed |
| one Job model | largely implemented, with some legacy compatibility paths remaining |
| dogfooding | tooling exists, but most of the 24-task matrix remains unrun |

## What we have implemented

### Durable Jobs

DeadReckon can now:

- create a durable Job before starting provider work
- return one Job ID and detach
- preserve an append-only lifecycle history
- lease work to a local supervisor
- heartbeat and reclaim expired leases
- adopt an existing child rather than automatically starting another
- keep attempt, spend, wall-time and deadline limits
- report typed outcomes such as verified, blocked, cancelled, budget exhausted, needs review and failed
- supervise Single, Graph and Campaign work through the Job layer
- generate launchd and systemd user-service definitions

We also fixed crash-sensitive areas such as child creation and advanced Graph and Campaign recovery.

### The ordinary command journey

The main operator journey now centres on:

```text
start → status/attach → finish
       list
```

These commands use the same Job identity and `JobView`.

Ordinary runs, orchestration, supported chains, stored-plan forks and campaigns now have Job-backed routes. Some older commands remain compatibility paths, including historical chain resume and explicit uncontained or in-place execution.

### Two-key completion

Strict completion now requires:

1. deterministic definition-of-done checks to pass
2. an independent semantic judge to assess the goal, contract, diff and evidence

The semantic judge returns `achieved`, `revise` or `uncertain`.

A failed deterministic check cannot be overridden. An unavailable or uncertain strict judge stops for review.

We also fixed the Codex adapter so structured semantic answers survive JSONL parsing.

### Signed completion receipts

DeadReckon now creates an HMAC-SHA-256 receipt using signing material outside the agent workspace.

The receipt binds the result to:

- the approved goal and contract
- the effective policy
- the source and result revisions
- deterministic evidence
- the semantic judgment
- containment information
- the stop reason
- the Job and run identities

`finish` validates the receipt before recording delivery. Tampered receipts are refused.

### More truthful lifecycle handling

We fixed several cases where DeadReckon previously reported more certainty than it had:

- incomplete workspace cleanup no longer reports success
- synthetic completion evidence is rejected
- stale or inconsistent authority information fails closed in more places
- finished results are compared with the Git objects actually delivered
- private paths appearing anywhere in result history are rejected, even if later deleted

### Artifact isolation

The current uncommitted tranche adds a shared distinction between:

- deliverable code and documentation
- provider evidence
- trusted lifecycle metadata
- runtime-only files

This is being applied across:

- provider turns
- semantic diffs
- receipt indexes
- promotion
- Graph and Campaign composition
- plans
- inspection
- learning
- source-authority checks
- `finish`

Provider-created `.specstory`, `.deadreckon`, `target` and `node_modules` content is now filtered from deliverable results. Raw provider evidence remains available in provenance archives.

The turn loop also rewrites provider-created Git history onto the approved base, restores trusted lifecycle metadata and reattaches a detached branch.

### Dogfood and acceptance tooling

We now have:

- a 24-task multi-repository, multi-provider matrix
- a metrics collector
- a credential-free adversarial runner
- a detailed operator acceptance checklist
- tamper, supervisor-kill, worker-kill, restart and network-loss procedures

The credential-free suite currently records:

- 7 passed
- 0 failed
- 5 unproven

One real detached Codex Job completed with:

- the same durable ID throughout
- passing deterministic checks
- semantic `achieved`
- a valid HMAC receipt
- tamper rejection
- successful `finish`

However, that run exposed the provider-artifact problem. It therefore does not count as clean final acceptance evidence.

## What remains on the docket

### 1. Close the artifact security blockers

The current audits found several issues that prevent us calling the hardening tranche complete:

- ignored files and Git `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` flags can evade current cleanliness checks
- symlinks and gitlinks are not consistently indexed or copied
- a provider may be able to rewrite the linked-worktree `.git` control file
- non-UTF8 Git paths are decoded unsafely
- promotion has a crash window between moving the result and saving its new state
- some legacy recovery paths can still trust workspace routing metadata
- the semantic judge’s mutation guard is now too narrow
- apply verification checks signed paths but does not yet reject every unexpected extra committed path

These are real correctness and security problems, not polish.

### 2. Complete the missing tests

We still need direct tests for:

- a real process crash after provider completion but before sanitisation
- private artifacts hidden in merge history
- non-UTF8 paths
- deliverable symlinks
- Fresh, Copy, InPlace and Worktree ownership behaviour
- merge, squash, cherry-pick and already-applied finish strategies
- Graph and Campaign parent artifact boundaries
- macOS and Windows Git path behaviour

After those fixes, the full integrated `make verify` must pass. Current focused tests pass, but the whole uncommitted tranche has not yet passed final verification.

### 3. Repeat live interruption trials

We must still run real drills for:

- terminal closure
- worker death
- supervisor death and lease reclamation
- machine or user-service restart
- network loss
- Single, Graph and Campaign recovery
- duplicate-execution prevention
- lost-containment handling

### 4. Complete the dogfood matrix

The checked-in sanitized matrix currently has:

- 24 total tasks
- 2 attempted
- 22 not run
- 0 verified

We still need 20 to 30 credible tasks across repositories and providers, followed by measurement of recovery, intervention, false acceptance, false rejection, cost and result comprehension.

### 5. Finish integration and documentation

There are 12 Watchkeeper commits on local `main`. They have not been pushed to `origin/main`.

The artifact-isolation work is still unstaged in the shared workspace. It needs to be fixed, fully verified and committed before it joins those 12 commits.

After acceptance, we still need to update the architecture, changelog and public claims so they describe only what the trials proved.

The clearest summary is: DeadReckon now has the intended engine, judge, receipt and Job journey. What remains is proving that the boundaries survive hostile files, unusual Git histories and real process or machine interruption. [Watchkeeper acceptance checklist](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md)

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 10:21:13Z)**_

The diagnosis has now pinned the main causes:

- post-provider Git commands trust a writable worktree `.git` pointer
- receipts hash a filesystem projection that does not fully model Git paths, modes and links
- promotion publishes and deletes in the wrong durable order
- delivery compares only part of the applied delta
- several strict Job paths still fall back to agent-visible routing metadata

The existing authorization covers fixes. I’m splitting these by file boundary: one agent will harden Git control, one will make artifact copying and hashing type-aware, and one will repair promotion ordering. I’ll handle receipt-versus-Git equality and finish delivery centrally so those contracts stay coherent.

+fn retain_signed_result_revision(
+    state: &PipelineState,
+    job_id: &str,
+    revision: &str,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let record = read_run_codebase_record(&state.run_root, &state.working_dir)?;
+    if record.mode != CodebaseMode::Worktree {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    let git_root = record.source_git_root.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| {
+        completion_error(job_id, "worktree result is missing its source Git repository")
+    })?;
+    let ref_digest = sha256_text(job_id)
+        .strip_prefix("sha256:")
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| sha256_text(job_id).as_str())
+        .to_string();
+    let retention_ref = format!("refs/deadreckon/results/{ref_digest}");
+    let output = crate::git::run_git(
+        git_root,
+        &["update-ref", &retention_ref, revision, "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"],
+    )?;
+    if output.status.success() {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    let existing = git_revision(git_root, &retention_ref)?;
+    if existing.as_deref() == Some(revision) {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    require_git_success(git_root, &output, "retain signed result revision")
+}

+
+fn workspace_git_control_identity(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<String> {
+    let git = working_dir.join(".git");
+    let metadata = match fs::symlink_metadata(&git) {
+        Ok(metadata) => metadata,
+        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
+            return Ok("missing".to_string());
+        }
+        Err(source) => {
+            return Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
+                path: git,
+                source,
+            });
+        }
+    };
+    if metadata.file_type().is_file() {
+        return deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&git)
+            .map(|hash| format!("file:{hash}"));
+    }
+    if metadata.file_type().is_dir() {
+        let hash =
+            deadreckon_core::flight::build_workspace_guard_file_index(&git)?.tree_hash();
+        return Ok(format!("directory:{hash}"));
+    }
+    Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+        "semantic judge refuses unsupported Git control entry {}",
+        git.display()
+    )))
+}

The first central hardening change is now in place: strict Worktree receipts materialise the signed Git revision into a clean temporary checkout and compare the complete deliverable index with the actual result. They also reject masked index entries and retain the signed commit under a dedicated Git ref so cleanup cannot make it disappear. I have also tightened `finish` so it refuses extra committed paths introduced during apply, and strict lifecycle commands no longer fall back to workspace routing metadata. Tests are being added alongside each invariant.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 10:43:11Z)**_

Short version: we have built most of the Watchkeeper machinery, but we have not yet earned the final product claim. The remaining work is primarily integration, adversarial verification, and real-world dogfooding.

## What the loop implemented

| Original objective | Current state |
|---|---|
| Durable goal executor | Jobs are persisted before work starts, receive one durable ID, detach from the caller, use leases and heartbeats, recover abandoned attempts, supervise process groups, and retain bounded retry, spend, wall-time and deadline policies. |
| Explicit outcomes | Jobs distinguish verified, blocked, cancelled, budget exhausted, retry exhausted, needs review and fatal failure. Cleanup failures are reported honestly. |
| Semantic meta-judge | Deterministic checks run first. A separate semantic judge then returns `achieved`, `revise` or `uncertain`. Failed checks cannot be overridden, and strict judge failure becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`. |
| Tamper-resistant completion | HMAC-signed receipts bind the goal, contract, policy, source, result, deterministic evidence, semantic judgment, containment and stop reason. Synthetic markers are rejected. |
| One job model | Supported single runs, graphs, chains and campaigns now travel through the durable Job scheduler and project a common `JobView`. `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list` and `finish` use that model. Some historical and explicitly uncontained paths remain compatibility modes. |
| Crash recovery | Child launch/linking is crash-atomic, expired leases can be reclaimed, advanced graph/campaign state can be reconstructed, and service definitions exist for launchd and systemd-user. |
| Operator evidence | We added the 24-task dogfood kit, fault injection tests, adversarial trials, metrics collection, architecture documentation and an [operator acceptance script](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md). |

## The hardening work completed today

The three parallel workstreams have now finished their scoped implementation:

- Artifact identity now includes symlinks, executable bits, file contents and raw platform path identity. Special files fail closed.
- Provider processes are denied access to the real Git control directories. A redirected `.git` file is detected, archived and restored; sanitizer commands use explicitly trusted Git paths.
- The receipt now proves that the signed Git revision and delivered filesystem are the same result, including ignored and hidden-index changes.
- `finish` refuses extra delivered paths that were not in the signed result.
- Semantic judging detects workspace, lifecycle, evidence and `.git` mutation.
- Promotion is now a recoverable state machine: validate candidate, publish, validate again, save state, then remove only an owned workspace.
- Promotion recovery covers crashes before rename, after rename, after state save and older stale-state layouts.
- Signed result commits receive retained Git references so cleanup cannot make the receipt’s commit disappear.

Focused tests for those individual areas are green, including 20 completion-boundary tests, 10 promotion tests, sandbox tests and the `.git` redirection/restart attack.

## Where the code currently is

There are 12 Watchkeeper commits on the local `main`, from `79bb2e8` through `080a5eb`. Local `main` is 12 commits ahead of `origin/main`; nothing has been pushed.

The latest hardening tranche is also in the same shared local worktree—there are no separate subagent branches to merge. It currently changes 22 source files with roughly 5,150 inserted lines. It is not committed yet because it still needs integration review and whole-repository verification.

## What is still on the docket

1. Finish integration review of the hardening tranche.

   One sanitizer history scanner still needs to become merge-aware and byte-safe. We also need focused tests for non-UTF-8 paths, merge topology, semantic-judge mutation and Git submodule/gitlink behavior.

2. Run the complete quality gate.

   That means formatting, focused tests, workspace Clippy, the full test suite and `make verify`. Then commit the hardening tranche using exact source-file staging while leaving the unrelated workspace changes untouched.

3. Repeat real provider trials.

   The checked-in matrix currently records:

   - 24 tasks defined
   - 2 attempted
   - 22 not run
   - 0 checked-in verified completions

   A later disposable Codex run completed but exposed provider-private artifact leakage, so we deliberately did not count it as acceptance evidence. That discovery caused the current hardening pass.

4. Prove interruption recovery outside fixtures.

   The credential-free suite has 7 passing trials, but these five live claims remain unproven:

   - kill a real provider worker and recover;
   - restart the supervisor during real work;
   - remove network access during a provider call;
   - reboot with an installed user service;
   - run a hostile cross-provider gate attack.

5. Complete the dogfood matrix and metrics.

   We still need unattended-completion rates, recovery rates, operator intervention counts, judging cost, comprehension time and human-reviewed false acceptance/rejection results.

6. Reconcile final documentation and claims.

   The architecture map and operator guide exist, but the CHANGELOG and public wording must be checked against what the completed trials actually prove.

So the honest assessment is: the core system is implemented, and the latest trust-boundary weaknesses now have code fixes. What remains is to integrate that work cleanly and demonstrate—through real interruptions and the remaining 22 tasks—that the system consistently keeps its promise.

+fn default_sandbox_toml(state: &PipelineState) -> SandboxToml {
+    let mut tools = BTreeMap::new();
+    for name in ["bash", "write_file"] {
+        tools.insert(
+            name.to_string(),
+            SandboxTomlTool {
+                read: vec![state.working_dir.clone()],

+    }
+    SandboxToml { version: 1, tools }
+}
+
+fn approved_sandbox_toml(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<Option<SandboxToml>> {
+    let paths = paths_for_state(state)?;
+    if !paths.job_json(&state.run_id).is_file() {
+        return Ok(None);
+    }
+    let job = deadreckon_core::load_job(&paths, &state.run_id)?;
+    let authority_path = paths.job_authority(&state.run_id);
+    if deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&authority_path)? != job.authority_sha256 {
+        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "Job authority changed before execution policy materialization".to_string(),
+        ));
+    }
+    let authority_raw = std::fs::read(&authority_path).with_path(&authority_path)?;
+    let authority: JobAuthority =
+        serde_json::from_slice(&authority_raw).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
+            path: authority_path,
+            source,
+        })?;
+    let policy_raw =
+        serde_json::to_string(&job.policy).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
+            path: paths.job_json(&state.run_id),
+            source,
+        })?;
+    if deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(&policy_raw) != authority.effective_policy_sha256 {
+        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "Job execution policy no longer matches approved authority".to_string(),
+        ));
+    }
+    let execution = job.policy.execution.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
+        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "Job predates immutable execution policy; refusing unattended execution".to_string(),
+        )
+    })?;
+    if !execution.require_containment
+        || execution.sandbox_requested != authority.sandbox_requested
+    {
+        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "Job containment policy no longer matches approved authority".to_string(),
+        ));
+    }
+    let tools = execution
+        .tools
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(name, tool)| {
+            (
+                name.clone(),
+                SandboxTomlTool {
+                    read: tool
+                        .workspace_read
+                        .then(|| state.working_dir.clone())
+                        .into_iter()
+                        .collect(),
+                    write: tool
+                        .workspace_write
+                        .then(|| state.working_dir.clone())
+                        .into_iter()
+                        .collect(),
+                    network: tool.network_allowlist.clone(),
+                },
+            )
+        })
+        .collect();
+    Ok(Some(SandboxToml { version: 1, tools }))
+}
+

+fn refuse_gitlinks(control: &TrustedGitControl) -> Result<()> {
+    let output = trusted_git_output(control, &["ls-files", "--stage", "-z", "--"])?;
+    if !output.status.success() {
+        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "git index-kind inventory failed: {}{}",
+            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
+            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+        )));
+    }
+    let gitlinks = output
+        .stdout
+        .split(|byte| *byte == 0)
+        .filter(|entry| !entry.is_empty())
+        .filter_map(|entry| {

+
+    output.extend_from_slice(path.as_os_str().as_bytes());
+    Ok(())
+}

+#[cfg(not(unix))]
+fn append_git_path_bytes(output: &mut Vec<u8>, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {

+        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(

+fn trusted_git_output_with_input(
+    control: &TrustedGitControl,
+    args: &[&str],
+    input: &[u8],
+) -> Result<std::process::Output> {
+    restore_and_verify_git_control(control)?;
+    let git_dir = control.git_dir.to_str().ok_or_else(|| {
+        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "trusted Git directory {} is not UTF-8; refusing ambiguous command routing",
+            control.git_dir.display()
+        ))
+    })?;
+    let workspace = control.workspace.to_str().ok_or_else(|| {
+        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "trusted worktree {} is not UTF-8; refusing ambiguous command routing",
+            control.workspace.display()
+        ))
+    })?;
+    let git_dir_arg = format!("--git-dir={git_dir}");
+    let work_tree_arg = format!("--work-tree={workspace}");
+    let mut routed = Vec::with_capacity(args.len() + 2);
+    routed.push(git_dir_arg.as_str());
+    routed.push(work_tree_arg.as_str());
+    routed.extend_from_slice(args);
+    let output = run_git_with_input(&control.workspace, &routed, input)?;
+    restore_and_verify_git_control(control)?;
+    Ok(output)
+}

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 11:32:24Z)**_

The core Watchkeeper product now exists. DeadReckon can create durable Jobs, supervise isolated work, apply two-key verification, and produce signed receipts. What remains is mainly trust-boundary closure, orchestration parity, and proving the promise through real interruption and dogfood trials.

## What we have implemented

| Area | Current achievement |
|---|---|
| Durable Job model | One Job ID, immutable authority, append-only events, rebuildable projection, attempts, leases and typed terminal outcomes. |
| Detached execution | `start` records the Job before execution and launches a detached supervisor. Closing the terminal does not inherently cancel it. |
| Recovery | Lease fencing, stale-lease reclaim, process-group supervision, guarded child launch, same-ID Plan/Campaign recovery and bounded retry/budget handling. |
| Two-key completion | Deterministic checks run first. Only then does a fresh, read-only semantic judge assess whether the result actually meets the goal. |
| Semantic outcomes | `achieved`, `revise` and `uncertain` exist. Unavailable or uncertain strict judgment becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`, not verified. |
| Tamper-resistant receipt | HMAC-SHA-256 receipt binds the approved goal, contract, policy, source, result, deterministic proof, semantic judgment and containment. |
| Gate protection | Signing keys live outside the agent workspace. Authority, gate, proof and receipt paths are protected. Synthetic or forged markers are rejected. |
| Common operator surface | `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list` and `finish` understand Jobs. Direct runs, orchestration, stored-plan forks, supported chains and campaigns now enter the Job scheduler. |
| Safe promotion | Receipt validation is required before trusted promotion. Promotion has idempotent recovery across several crash windows. |
| Service support | launchd and systemd-user definitions plus supervisor install/start/status/stop commands exist. |
| Documentation | Watchkeeper is documented in the MAP, AS-BUILT architecture, README, Concepts, CHANGELOG and an operator acceptance script. |
| Test infrastructure | Fault tests, adversarial tests, a 24-task dogfood matrix, metrics collector and human-review template exist. |

The current uncommitted hardening work adds:

- Exact result identity against the signed Git revision.
- Detection of ignored, dirty, assume-unchanged and skip-worktree files.
- Merge-aware detection of protected paths hidden in result history.
- Non-UTF-8 path handling.
- Executable-bit, symlink and raw symlink-target identity.
- Explicit refusal of unsupported Git submodules.
- Protection of the real Git directory, including linked worktrees.
- An isolated, read-only documentation provider.
- Semantic-judge mutation checks even when the judge times out or fails.
- Binding the effective sandbox and tool policy into approved authority.
- Crash-safe promotion ordering and recovery.

That tranche currently passes `cargo check`, but has not yet passed the complete verification pipeline.

## What is still on the docket

### 1. Finish and integrate the current hardening tranche

- Complete Git-filter refusal on the receipt-verification side.
- Close remaining `finish` issues around non-UTF paths, deleted delivery paths and rollback after a failed post-apply check.
- Run formatting, focused tests, Clippy and full `make verify`.
- Commit the tranche cleanly.

### 2. Fully earn the machine-survival claim

The detached supervisor survives the launching terminal, but that is not the same as surviving a machine restart.

Still needed:

- Refuse unattended durable starts when no restart-capable service is installed.
- Perform real worker-kill and supervisor-kill drills.
- Test actual launchd/systemd service recovery.
- Perform at least one real reboot/login recovery trial.

### 3. Complete scheduler parity

The major execution shapes use Jobs, but some old machinery remains underneath.

Still needed:

- Make semantic `revise` continue Graph and Campaign work instead of stopping for review.
- Decide whether remaining historical chain, preview and uncontained paths should be adapted or deliberately retained as legacy.
- Improve Campaign/Graph aggregate attempt, spend and delivery reporting.
- Continue collapsing lifecycle truth around one Job history.

### 4. Complete the fault and adversarial matrix

Every durable boundary should have deterministic failure injection:

- lease;
- spawn;
- child linkage;
- gate;
- semantic judge;
- receipt sealing;
- promotion and delivery.

Live trials must also cover network loss, worker termination, supervisor termination, gate tampering and cross-provider attacks.

### 5. Run the actual dogfood program

The matrix contains 24 tasks, but only 2 have been attempted, 22 remain unrun, and 0 have reached verified completion.

We therefore do not yet know:

- unattended verified-completion rate;
- automatic recovery rate;
- false acceptance or rejection rate;
- operator intervention rate;
- supervision and judging cost;
- how quickly a human can understand the final receipt.

### 6. Reconcile final public claims

Once the behavior and trials settle, the documentation needs one final pass so it distinguishes:

- implemented from live-proven;
- terminal survival from machine survival;
- contained verified Jobs from compatibility execution;
- Single revision support from Graph/Campaign revision support.

## Where the work currently lives

Everything is in the shared repository working tree on local `main`:

- Local `main` is 12 commits ahead of `origin/main`.
- Those commits have not been pushed.
- The newest hardening tranche is still uncommitted: roughly 6,252 additions across 33 tracked code/test files.
- Subagents did not create separate hidden branches; their changes entered this same working tree.

The governing documents are [Watchkeeper goal](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-07-28-2321-deadreckon-watchkeeper-goal.md), [Watchkeeper rider](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-07-28-2321-deadreckon-watchkeeper-rider.md), [current map](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md), and [operator acceptance](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md).

My plain assessment: the architecture and core feature set are substantially built. The statement “give it a goal and it will reliably run until independently verified” is implemented as a system design, but it has not yet been earned as an operational guarantee. The critical path now is to finish the hardening tranche, run full verification, and dogfood interruption recovery—not add more product surface.

name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
---

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-30 11:33:18Z)**_

The remaining causes are now localized:

- The run sanitizer refuses active Git filters before staging in `turn_loop.rs`, but the receipt verifier later calls `checkout-index` in `completion.rs` without the same check. A signed `.gitattributes` file can therefore make trusted verification execute an operator-configured smudge command.
- `finish` compares delivered tree entries using a UTF-8 pathspec, even though the upstream Git inventories correctly preserve raw path bytes.
- More seriously, `finish` verifies only after it has merged and restored the operator stash. If that verification fails, the target branch has already moved, so a refused delivery can still remain applied.

I’ll verify the filter fix with a sentinel command that must never execute, raw non-UTF filenames on Unix, and a forced post-merge mismatch that must restore the target revision.

+fn git_history_paths(git_root: &Path, base: &str, result: &str) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {
+    require_git_ancestor(git_root, base, result)?;
+    let revisions = git_revisions(git_root, base, result)?;
+    let mut paths = BTreeSet::new();
+    for revision in revisions {
+        let output = crate::git::run_git(
+            git_root,
+            &[
+                "diff-tree",
+                "--root",
+                "--no-commit-id",
+                "--name-only",
+                "--no-renames",
+                "-r",
+                "-m",
+                "-z",
+                &revision,
+                "--",
+            ],
+        )?;
+        require_git_success(git_root, &output, "inspect result commit paths")?;
+        paths.extend(nul_paths(&output.stdout)?);
+    }
+    Ok(paths.into_iter().collect())
+}

+fn rollback_refused_job_delivery(

+        ));
+    }
+    if let Some(stash) = autostash

+        return CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(

+                stash.refname
+            ),
+            &format!(
+                "inspect `git status`, then recover the operator changes with `git stash pop {}`",
+                stash.refname
+            ),
+        ));
+    }

# Map of DeadReckon

Status: repository analysis updated 2026-07-30 through the Watchkeeper
recovery/budget hardening and credential-free adversarial trials.

## Executive map

DeadReckon is not primarily another coding agent. It is an outer control plane for coding agents and agent harnesses. The inner harness proposes and performs work; DeadReckon owns the durable run, isolation, budgets, evidence, independent completion decision, recovery, and promotion.

Its irreducible pattern is:

```text
goal + definition of done
          |
          v
isolated, durable Job -----> provider / inner harness does work
          |                              |
          +<---- events, spend, diffs, snapshots, provenance
          |
          v
contained checks + independent semantic judge
          |
          +---- fail/revise: retain evidence, continue or stop explicitly
          |
          +---- pass: seal receipt, then promote deliberately
```

That is the essential product. The strongest reason for it to exist is the gap between *an agent saying it is done* and *an operator being able to trust, inspect, recover, and accept the result*. This matches the original unmet-needs research: predictable delegation needed operational infrastructure more than another transcript or chat surface.

The repository now contains three different things which should not be judged alike:

1. A differentiated Job kernel: immutable authority, append-only lifecycle,
   fenced local supervision and isolated work across guided and ordinary
   direct execution. Durable Single, Graph and Campaign Jobs prove 2
   independent completion decisions before deliberate promotion. Preserve and
   dogfood this.
2. Established graph/campaign conductors, direct advanced commands, reports,
   imports, and narration. Ordinary direct orchestration, new chains,
   stored-plan forks and campaigns now run those conductors under a parent Job
   and verify the merged parent. Explicit compatibility modes and chain
   extension remain process-owned.
3. Compatibility layers, speculative depth, and incomplete bets. Deprecate or
   quarantine these rather than allowing them to obscure the kernel.

## How maturity is assessed

Maturity here means engineering evidence in this repository, not market adoption.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Hardened** | Central path, persistent model, broad tests, recovery/error semantics and established user surface. |
| **Stable / bounded** | Real and tested, but deliberately narrower than the whole unmet need. |
| **Maturing** | Substantive implementation with a known parity, safety, migration or operability gap. |
| **Experimental** | Working implementation whose product demand or abstraction boundary is not yet established. |
| **Compatibility-only** | Retained for old scripts or naming; not a product direction. |
| **Absent** | The underlying need is not currently addressed, even if nearby primitives exist. |

The repository has extensive automated coverage, but it has no product-usage telemetry. A feature can therefore be engineering-mature and still be unvalidated as something operators need.

## Architecture: the six layers

| Layer | Main location | Responsibility | Product significance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operator surface | `crates/deadreckon` | CLI, guided `start`, Course, lifecycle commands, attach, orchestration entry points | Keeps the default flow approachable while exposing advanced control. |
| Runtime | `crates/deadreckon-runtime` | Outer turn loop, provider/sandbox composition, process execution, flight recording, docs and seams | Enforces policy around an inner harness rather than trusting that harness to supervise itself. |
| Core | `crates/deadreckon-core` | Job event store/reducer, fenced leases, process groups, receipts, paths, run state, gates, promotion and `RunView`/`JobView` | Durable source of truth and most of the product's invariants. |
| Providers | `crates/deadreckon-providers` | Provider trait/router, direct HTTP models, concrete CLIs, descriptor-driven CLIs and Codex app-server support | Makes the control vocabulary portable across changing agent harnesses. |
| Sandbox | `crates/deadreckon-sandbox` | Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Docker and explicit no-sandbox execution | Creates the capability boundary between delegated work and the host. |
| Protocol | `crates/deadreckon-protocol` | Versioned run ledgers plus checked Job, lease, authority, semantic-judgment and completion-receipt wire types | Separates durable evidence from implementation internals. |

The intended dependency direction is operator surface -> runtime -> provider/sandbox/core -> protocol. Keel moved the persisted ledger types, readers and writers onto that downward dependency and added checked schemas without changing the stored bytes.

From the beginning of the Watchkeeper loop, we have built most of the core architecture. We have not yet completed the operational proof needed to make the full promise confidently.

## Implemented

- A durable `Job` identity with immutable launch policy and approved definition of done.
- An append-only job event history with typed phases and stop reasons.
- A local supervisor that leases jobs, heartbeats, fences stale workers, and can recover abandoned attempts.
- Detached execution: supported starts can return an ID while work continues.
- Explicit outcomes including verified, blocked, cancelled, failed, budget exhausted, deadline reached, retry exhausted, and needs review.
- Process-group supervision and crash-atomic child launching.
- Budgets for spend, time, attempts, and deadlines retained across recovery.
- A common Job lifecycle for supported Single, Graph, Chain, stored-plan, and Campaign launches.
- The ordinary `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list`, and `finish` journey over Jobs.
- Two-key completion:

  1. Deterministic definition-of-done checks must pass.
  2. A fresh, read-only semantic judge must decide that the result actually achieves the goal.

- Semantic `uncertain` or unavailable results stop at `NEEDS_REVIEW`.
- Semantic `revise` can return an ordinary Single Job to execution.
- HMAC-SHA-256 completion receipts with signing keys outside the agent workspace.
- Receipts bound to the goal, contract, execution policy, source revision, result revision, deterministic proof, semantic judgment, and containment.
- Promotion and `finish` revalidate the receipt and exact result instead of trusting an agent’s “done” message.
- Transactional promotion recovery and rollback when delivery verification fails.
- Extensive trust-boundary hardening:

  - protected `.git` and DeadReckon control paths;
  - hostile provider commit removal;
  - trusted DeadReckon-owned commits;
  - read-only documentation and semantic providers;
  - symlink and executable-mode identity;
  - raw/non-UTF-8 path handling;
  - merge-aware delivery history;
  - rejection of Git submodules/gitlinks;
  - refusal to execute Git clean/smudge filters during trusted verification;
  - detection of paths added and later deleted to conceal delivery side effects.

- Launchd and systemd-user service definitions and management commands.
- A 24-task dogfood matrix, metrics collector, human-review format, and credential-free adversarial harness.
- Updated architecture, operator-acceptance, README, schema, and map documentation.

## Current integration state

There are 12 Watchkeeper commits on the local `main` branch, ahead of `origin/main`. They have not been pushed.

There is also a large hardening tranche still uncommitted:

- 35 tracked files changed;
- roughly 6,800 insertions;
- one new source file, `artifact_policy.rs`.

So the work presently has two layers:

1. A substantial committed foundation on local `main`.
2. Current trust-boundary and promotion hardening still in the shared working tree.

## Immediate unfinished work

The current hardening exposed a cleanup regression. Runtime build output such as `target/` is correctly excluded from trusted result commits, but Git then refuses to remove the worktree because that output remains untracked.

This currently causes eight broader integration tests to fail. The intended fix is narrow: remove only known runtime residue such as untracked `target/` and `node_modules/`, while continuing to preserve and refuse deletion of unknown operator files.

After that:

- rerun the broader codebase suite;
- run workspace checks, Clippy, formatting, and full `make verify`;
- commit the hardening tranche as one reviewed unit.

## Still on the docket

The important remaining product work is:

- Enforce the persistent-service preflight. A noninteractive durable start should refuse when no restart-capable user service is installed. The current detached process survives a terminal, but that is not the same as surviving a reboot.
- Prove real machine-restart recovery, not merely service-definition and simulated-restart tests.
- Let Graph and Campaign parents safely resume after semantic `revise`; today they stop honestly at `NEEDS_REVIEW`.
- Complete receipt/report narration for attempts, total spend and time, revisions, containment, and final delivery.
- Expand the auditable fault matrix across spawn, child linking, gate execution, semantic judging, receipt sealing, and promotion.
- Run the live 24-task dogfood matrix. Only two tasks have been attempted, neither produced a verified receipt, and 22 remain unrun.
- Perform live hostile trials:

  - kill the worker;
  - kill the supervisor;
  - reboot the machine;
  - remove network access;
  - tamper with gate and receipt paths;
  - exercise multiple providers and sandbox backends.

- Collect false-acceptance, false-rejection, intervention, recovery, cost, and comprehension metrics.
- Reconcile contradictory documentation around direct versus compatibility execution paths.
- Decide which legacy process-owned chain/campaign modes remain supported and which should be retired.

The honest assessment is: the durable job kernel, two-key verification, protected receipt, unified scheduling, and deliberate promotion machinery largely exist. What remains is closing the current cleanup regression, integrating the hardening work, and proving the system through real interruption and dogfood trials. Only after those trials can we responsibly make the full claim:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify both the checks and the meaning of the result, and leave behind a clear receipt explaining what happened.

name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
